questions.q: Q.1) Consider the following statements: 1️⃣ The First Battle of Panipat, 1526 is a landmark event known for the fundamental shift it introduced in the nature of Indian warfare. 2️⃣ The First Battle of Panipat was characterised by the utilization of two revolutionary concepts of Artillery and the Tulughma (flanking maneuver).
o: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct and Statement II explains Statement I
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Both Statement I and Statement II are correct but Statement II does not explain Statement I
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
questions.e: The establishment of Mughal rule in 1526 was a transformative event because it introduced the "Gunpowder Age" to India. In the First Battle of Panipat, Babur utilized revolutionary concepts of Artillery (cannons and matchlocks) and the Tulughma (flanking maneuver). Despite being outnumbered, these tactical superiorities allowed Babur to defeat Ibrahim Lodi, proving that modern technology was superior to sheer numerical strength.

questions.q: Q.2) With regard to the Vijayanagar Empire, consider the following statements: 1️⃣ It was established in the 14th century on the southern bank of the Tungabhadra River. 2️⃣ The empire was founded by Harihara I and Bukka Raya I, from the Sangama dynasty.
questions.e: The Vijayanagar Empire was established in 1336 CE (14th century) on the southern bank of the Tungabhadra River in modern-day Karnataka. It was founded by two brothers, Harihara I and Bukka Raya I, who belonged to the Sangama dynasty. They were originally feudatories of the Kakatiyas of Warangal.

questions.q: Q.3) With reference to the Baburnama, consider the following statements: 1️⃣ It was written by Babur himself in Persian language. 2️⃣ It provides a detailed description of flora and fauna of the plains of North India. 3️⃣ It gives accounts of battles, strategies, and the introduction of gunpowder tactics.
questions.e: The Baburnama is the autobiography of Zahir-ud-din Muhammad Babur. It was originally written in Chagatai Turkic, his native language, not Persian. The work provides vivid descriptions of the natural world, including the flora and fauna of North India. It also contains detailed military accounts of battles and the introduction of gunpowder tactics.

questions.q: Q.4) Which one of the following political developments in medieval India occurred first?
o: Establishment of the Gajapati kingdom of Orissa
Emergence of the Sultanate of Golconda
Emergence of the Sultanates of Ahmadnagar, Bijapur and Berar
Conquest of Goa by the Portuguese
questions.e: Chronologically, the Gajapati kingdom of Orissa was established in 1435. The Sultanates of Ahmadnagar, Bijapur, and Berar emerged later in 1490. The Portuguese conquered Goa in 1510, and the Sultanate of Golconda emerged in 1518.

questions.q: Q.5) How many of the following areas were contested between Vijayanagar rulers and the Bahmani sultans? 1️⃣ Raichur doab 2️⃣ Krishna-Godavari delta 3️⃣ Konkan coast 4️⃣ Cauvery delta
questions.e: The interests of Vijayanagar and Bahmani rulers clashed in three distinct areas: the Tungabhadra (Raichur) Doab, the Krishna-Godavari Delta, and the Marathwada country (Konkan Coast) . The Cauvery delta was primarily under Chola influence and not a major point of contention between these two specific powers.

questions.q: Q.6) Consider the following statements with regard to Humayun: 1️⃣ He fought the Battle of Sirhind (1555 AD) with Rana Sanga to establish Mughal rule in India. 2️⃣ He laid the foundation of Dinpanah which is recognized as the "Sixth City of Delhi."
questions.e: Humayun's victory at the Battle of Sirhind  was against Sikandar Suri, not Rana Sanga. This victory re-established Mughal rule. He also founded the city of Dinpanah in 1533, which is recognized as the "Sixth City of Delhi".

questions.q: Q.7) Consider the following statements: 1️⃣ Statement I: The Mughal annexation of the Sultanates of Bijapur and Golconda in the 1680s accelerated the collapse of Mughal authority in the region. 2️⃣ Statement II: The destruction of these Deccan Sultanates brought the Mughal army into a direct and prolonged confrontation with the Marathas.
o: Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Both Statement I and Statement II are correct and Statement II is the correct explanation for Statement I
Both Statement I and Statement II are correct and Statement II is the correct explanation for Statement I
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
questions.e: Aurangzeb annexed Bijapur  and Golconda , but this proved to be a "pyrrhic victory" as administering such a vast, hostile territory led to a breakdown in imperial efficiency . Historically, the Sultanates had acted as a barrier; their removal brought the Mughals into a 27-year war with the Marathas, which drained the treasury and led to the empire's disintegration .

questions.q: Q.8) Which one of the following statements about French traveller François Bernier is not correct?
o: He observed that the people in Mughal India owned and transferred private property.
He observed that there was a lack of interest in Western scientific discoveries.
He recorded his observations in his seminal work 'Travels in the Mogul Empire'.
He described Indian society as having "no middle state".
questions.e: François Bernier observed that Mughal India lacked private property, believing the Emperor was the sole owner of all land . This "crown ownership," he argued, discouraged long-term agricultural investment. He correctly recorded his work in 'Travels in the Mogul Empire', noted the lack of a "middle state," and observed a lack of interest in Western science.

questions.q: Q.9) With reference to the Bahmani Kingdom, consider the following statements: 1️⃣ It was founded by Alauddin Hasan Bahman Shah, with the capital at Bidar. 2️⃣ Prime Minister Mahmud Gawan reorganized the kingdom into eight tarafs.
questions.e: The Bahmani Kingdom was founded by Alauddin Hasan Bahman Shah in 1347, but the initial capital was Gulbarga (Ahsanabad), not Bidar. The capital was shifted to Bidar later in 1425 by Ahmad Shah I Wali. Prime Minister Mahmud Gawan did reorganize the kingdom into eight smaller provinces called tarafs.

questions.q: Q.10) How many of the following statements regarding the economic reforms of Sher Shah are correct? 1️⃣ He introduced a silver coin known as the Rupiya which became the precursor to the modern Indian Rupee. 2️⃣ He introduced written documents Patta, a title-deed defining land area and tax. 3️⃣ He constructed the Grand Trunk road from Bengal to Punjab. 4️⃣ He introduced the Sikandari Gaz for uniform land measurement.
questions.e: Sher Shah introduced the silver Rupiya and the Patta (title-deed) along with the Qabuliyat. He used the Sikandari Gaz for uniform land measurement. While he revived and extended the ancient route from Sonargaon to the Indus (Grand Trunk Road), Statement III is often considered correct in general context, though the solution suggests only three statements are correct without specifying the error.

questions.q: Q.11) Consider the following statements with regard to Vidyaranya: 1️⃣ He was the 12th Jagadguru of the Sringeri Sharada Peetham in the 14th century. 2️⃣ He served as a prime minister to the first three generations of Vijayanagar kings. 3️⃣ He guided the selection and planning of the capital city, Vidyanagara, at the site of Hampi.
questions.e: Vidyaranya was the 12th Jagadguru of Sringeri Sharada Peetham (1380–1386 CE). He served as a senior minister and advisor to the first three Vijayanagar rulers: Harihara I, Bukka Raya I, and Harihara II . He also guided the planning of the capital city, Vidyanagara (later Vijayanagar), at Hampi .

questions.q: Q.12) In the medieval times, the ports of Chaul and Dabhol served as the principle ports of:
questions.e: Chaul and Dabhol, located on the Konkan Coast, were the principal ports of the Bahmani Kingdom. Dabhol was the most prosperous port and served as a primary naval base. These ports facilitated trade with the Persian Gulf and Red Sea, including the critical import of Arabian horses .

questions.q: Q.13) How many of the following statements regarding the administration of Sher Shah Suri are correct? 1️⃣ Sarkars and Parganas were units of local administration. 2️⃣ Muqaddams were personally held responsible for crimes committed in their jurisdiction. 3️⃣ He revived Alauddin Khalji's Dagh (branding of horses) and Chehra (descriptive rolls of soldiers). 4️⃣ The network of Sarais was used to establish an efficient postal service.
questions.e: Sher Shah divided the empire into Sarkars and Parganas . He held Muqaddams (village headmen) personally responsible for local crimes. He revived the Dagh and Chehra systems for military discipline and used Sarais as dak-chowkis for an efficient postal service .

questions.q: Q.14) Consider the following statements with regard to the Second Battle of Panipat : 1️⃣ It was fought between the Mughal forces led by Akbar and the Afghan forces led by Sher Shah Suri. 2️⃣ It resulted in the re-establishment of Mughal authority in North India after a period of exile.
questions.e: The Second Battle of Panipat  was fought between Akbar (led by Bairam Khan) and the Hindu King Hemu, who was the Chief Minister of Adil Shah Suri—not Sher Shah Suri himself. The victory re-established Mughal authority in North India and ensured the empire's survival.

questions.q: Q.15) In the context of medieval India, Rayasam, Karanikkam and Sarvanayaka refers to:
o: senior officials in the Vijayanagar empire
special rituals for the coronation of king
duties levied on import of goods
questions.e: These were important officials in the Vijayanagar secretariat. Rayasam was the secretary who dispatched king's orders , Karanikkam was an accountant , and Sarvanayaka (or Maneyapradhana) was the officer of the royal household.

questions.q: Q.16) During the Mughal rule, qanungos and karoris were:
questions.e: Qanungos were hereditary keepers of land records at the Pargana level. Karoris were revenue collectors introduced by Akbar, each appointed to a district expected to yield one crore dams. Together, they managed tax assessment and collection.

questions.q: Q.17) With reference to the Dahsala system, consider the following statements: 1️⃣ It was a ten-year settlement of land revenue. 2️⃣ The revenue demand was fixed at one-third of the average produce, calculated in cash. 3️⃣ Bamboo Jarib and the Gaz-i-Ilahi were utilized as a standardized measurement system to ensure accuracy.
questions.e: The Dahsala system was based on the average produce and prices of the preceding ten years , but it was not a permanent ten-year settlement as the state could modify it. The demand was fixed at one-third of the average produce in cash , and it used a standardized Bamboo Jarib and Gaz-i-Ilahi.

questions.q: Q.18) It was the highest and most productive category of land classification in medieval India. It was a land that was continuously cultivated for every crop in succession and was never allowed to lie fallow. Which one of the following is referred to in the above description?
questions.e: In the Dahsala system, Polaj was the highest category of land, continuously cultivated and never left fallow . It was considered the best quality land due to high fertility. Parauti was left fallow for 1–2 years, while Chachar was left fallow for 3–4 years.

questions.q: Q.19) Consider the following statements: 1️⃣ Statement I: Mansabdari was an administrative system organized on a military basis. 2️⃣ Statement II: In the mansabdari system, officers were assigned both civil as well as military duties.
o: Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Both Statement I and Statement II are correct and Statement II explains Statement I
Both Statement I and Statement II are correct but Statement II does not explain Statement I
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
questions.e: Mansabdari was an administrative system organized on a military basis. It incorporated the army, nobility, and civil service into one order. Every official received a mansab (rank), and they were assigned both civil and military duties simultaneously .

questions.q: Q.20) Which of the following statements are correct with reference to the travellers who visited Vijayanagar empire? 1️⃣ Ibn Battuta had left accounts of the early years of Vijayanagar empire in his book Rehla. 2️⃣ Niccolò de' Conti provided early descriptions of the Vijayanagar city's fortifications. 3️⃣ Marco Polo provided detailed accounts of irrigation systems and efficient administration.
questions.e: Ibn Battuta visited during the early years (reign of Harihara I) and wrote the Rehla. Niccolò de' Conti visited around 1420-21 and described the city's fortifications. Marco Polo visited India in the 11th century, before the Vijayanagar Empire existed.

questions.q: Q.21) How many of the following statements regarding Firuz Shah Bahmani are correct? 1️⃣ He built an astronomical observatory at Daulatabad. 2️⃣ He founded the city of Firozabad on the banks of the Bhima River. 3️⃣ He defeated Deva Raya I in the Battle of Pangal (1419-1420). 4️⃣ He encouraged the settlement of Afaqis in Deccan who were foreigners from Persia and Central Asia.
questions.e: Firuz Shah Bahmani built an observatory at Daulatabad in 1407 and founded the city of Firozabad. He encouraged the settlement of "Afaqis" (foreigners). However, he was decisively defeated by Deva Raya I in the Battle of Pangal.

questions.q: Q.22) Which of the following states were known collectively as the Deccan Sultanates? 1️⃣ Adil Shahi of Bijapur 2️⃣ Khandesh Sultanate 3️⃣ Nizam Shahi of Ahmadnagar 4️⃣ Qutb Shahi of Golconda 5️⃣ Imad Shahi of Berar 6️⃣ Barid Shahi of Bidar
o: I, III, IV, V and VI only
I, II, V and VI only
II, III, IV and V only
I, II, III, IV and VI only
questions.e: The five Deccan Sultanates that emerged from the Bahmani Kingdom were Bijapur (Adil Shahi), Ahmadnagar (Nizam Shahi), Golconda (Qutb Shahi), Berar (Imad Shahi), and Bidar (Barid Shahi) . The Khandesh Sultanate was not considered one of the core five .

questions.q: Q.23) How many of the following pairs regarding land categories are correctly matched? 1️⃣ Khalisa: Income went directly to the royal exchequer 2️⃣ Inam: Allotted to learned and religious men 3️⃣ Jagir: Allotted to nobles and members of the royal family
questions.e: Khalisa land was directly administered, and its revenue went to the royal treasury . Inam lands were rent-free grants for scholars and religious men . Jagirs were revenue assignments given to nobles and military commanders in lieu of salary .

questions.q: Q.24) How many of the following pairs regarding Mughal offices are correctly matched? 1️⃣ Vakil: Finance Minister 2️⃣ Wazir: Prime Minister 3️⃣ Mir Bakhshi: Chief commander 4️⃣ Sadr-us-Sudur: Religious advisor
questions.e: Only Sadr-us-Sudur is correctly matched as the religious advisor and chief justice. The Vakil was the Prime Minister (later ornamental). The Wazir was the head of the finance department. Mir Bakhshi was the minister in charge of the army/nobility records, not the chief commander.

questions.q: Q.25) How many of the following pairs regarding Mughal administrative units are correctly matched? 1️⃣ Subah: Siqqadar 2️⃣ Sarkars: Faujdar 3️⃣ Parganas: Chaudhuri 4️⃣ Village: Muqaddam
questions.e: A Subah (province) was headed by a Subedar, not a Siqqadar . Sarkars were in the charge of a Faujdar. Parganas had officers like the Chaudhuri for revenue collection. The Village was under a Muqaddam.

questions.q: Q.26) How many of the following statements regarding the economy of the Vijayanagar Empire are correct? 1️⃣ In the Hampi Bazaar, merchants openly sold rubies, diamonds, emeralds, and pearls. 2️⃣ Nen pudavai and parum pudavai were handcrafted ornaments. 3️⃣ Pulicat on the Coromandel coast specialized in textile exports to Southeast Asia. 4️⃣ The gold coin known as the Varaha was the standard for international trade.
questions.e: Merchants sold precious stones in the Hampi Bazaar. Pulicat was a hub for textile exports , and the Varaha was the standard gold coin. However, Nen pudavai (fine muslins) and parum pudavai (coarse sarees) were types of textiles, not ornaments .

questions.q: Q.27) The book Adnyapatra, written by Ramchandrapant Amatya, deals with:
questions.e: Ramchandrapant Amatya served as the Finance Minister to Shivaji. His work 'Adnyapatra' reflects Shivaji's political ideals, principles, and policies of state administration (Swarajya) .

questions.q: Q.28) With reference to Akbar's religious policy, consider the following statements: 1️⃣ He established Ibadat Khana, the house of worship and inter-religious debate, at Fatehpur Sikri. 2️⃣ His principle of Sulh-i-Kul promoted a state that stood above religious and ethnic divisions. 3️⃣ Din-i-Ilahi was conceived more as a moral-ethical order than as an organised religion.
questions.e: Akbar established the Ibadat Khana in 1575 for inter-faith debates. Sulh-i-Kul meant "Absolute Peace" and promoted a state above religious divisions . Din-i-Ilahi  was an ethical code and syncretic spiritual path rather than a formal religion.

questions.q: Q.29) With reference to the judicial administration under Shivaji's rule, consider the following statements: 1️⃣ Manusmriti and Mitakshara were referred to as authorities in legal disputes. 2️⃣ Raj Sabha and Dharmasabha were judicial bodies. 3️⃣ All civil cases were decided by people's courts at the local level.
questions.e: Under the Marathas, legal authorities included Manusmriti and Mitakshara . Judicial bodies included the Raj Sabha (the most important) and Dharmasabha . Shivaji allowed civil and ordinary criminal cases to be decided by local people's courts.

questions.q: Q.30) How many of the following statements regarding Vijayanagar ruler Krishnadevaraya are correct? 1️⃣ He decisively defeated the combined forces of the Bahmani Sultans in the Battle of Diwani. 2️⃣ His court was adorned by Ashta Diggajas, eight celebrated poets of Telugu literature. 3️⃣ He described the ideal king's duties in his political treatise Amuktamalyada.
questions.e: Krishnadevaraya defeated the Bahmani forces in the Battle of Diwani . His court featured the Ashta Diggajas, pillars of Telugu literature. In his classic Telugu epic Amuktamalyada, he also detailed the political duties of an ideal king.

questions.q: Q.31) How many of the following statements are correct with reference to the alliance of Rajput rulers with Akbar? 1️⃣ These alliances were strictly military in nature. 2️⃣ The Rajput rulers were given Mansabs. 3️⃣ The Rajputs accepted the Mughal suzerainty. 4️⃣ The Rajputs transferred territorial rights over their ancestral lands.
questions.e: Akbar's alliances were not strictly military; they included matrimonial ties and administrative collaboration. While Rajputs accepted Mughal suzerainty , they did not transfer territorial rights; they kept internal control over their ancestral lands (Watan Jagirs).

questions.q: Q.32) With regard to the agriculture policy of Shivaji, how many of the following statements are not correct? 1️⃣ Deshmukhs collected taxes on behalf of the state. 2️⃣ A scientific method of land measurement known as the Kathi was introduced. 3️⃣ Tagai was the subsidized loans to farmers for purchasing cattle, seeds, and equipment.
questions.e: Only Statement I is incorrect because Shivaji abolished the system where middlemen like Deshmukhs collected taxes, replacing them with salaried government officials. He introduced the scientific Kathi system for land measurement and provided Tagai loans to farmers.

questions.q: Q.33) The Ayagar system was a unique feature of village organization and local administration in the:
questions.e: The Ayagar system was a unique feature of the Vijayanagar Empire. Each village was managed by a body of 12 functionaries (Ayagars), including the headman (Gauda), accountant (Karnam), and watchman (Talaiyari) .

questions.q: Q.34) How many of the following rows regarding Akbar's Navaratna are correctly matched? 1️⃣ Raja Todar Mal: Finance & Revenue, Introduced Zabt and Dahsala system 2️⃣ Tansen: Musician, Founded the Jaipur Gharana of Hindustani music 3️⃣ Raja Man Singh: Military General, Introduced field artillery 4️⃣ Abu al-Faiz Faizi: Poet, Translated Sanskrit text Lilavati into Persian
questions.e: Raja Todar Mal is correctly matched with finance and the Dahsala system. Faizi is correctly matched for translating Lilavati into Persian. Tansen founded the Gwalior Gharana, not Jaipur. Babur, not Man Singh, introduced field artillery.

questions.q: Q.35) Which of the statements given above regarding Shivaji are correct? 1️⃣ He started a new era Rajyabhisheka Shaka from the day of his coronation. 2️⃣ He minted gold coins "Shri Raja Shiv" on the obverse and "Chhatrapati" on the reverse in the Devanagari script. 3️⃣ Indian Navy's current ensign is inspired by the octagonal shape of Shivaji's royal seal.
questions.e: Shivaji started the Rajyabhisheka Shaka era upon his coronation in 1674. He minted gold coins (Hon) with Devanagari legends. The Indian Navy's current ensign is inspired by his octagonal royal seal.

questions.q: Q.36) Which of the following social reforms were introduced by Akbar? 1️⃣ Banned the practice of Sati 2️⃣ Fixed the minimum age of marriage for girls 3️⃣ Couples were required to register their marriages 4️⃣ Encouraged widow remarriage
questions.e: Akbar banned involuntary Sati and raised the minimum marriage age for girls to 14. He required couples to register marriages at the local kotwali and encouraged widow remarriage.

questions.q: Q.37) With reference to the Nayankara system of the Vijayanagar empire, consider the following statement: 1️⃣ It was a form of military feudalism that balanced central control with regional autonomy. 2️⃣ Jagir was the specific land or territory granted to Nayakas. 3️⃣ Nayakas were responsible for maintaining law and order and managing local infrastructure.
questions.e: The Nayankara system was a form of military feudalism. Nayakas were responsible for law, order, and infrastructure. However, the land granted to them was called Amaram, not Jagir (which is a Mughal term).

questions.q: Q.38) Which of the following crops/fruits were introduced in India during the Mughal rule? 1️⃣ Tobacco 2️⃣ Maize 3️⃣ Potato 4️⃣ Sugarcane 5️⃣ Cashew Nut 6️⃣ Pineapple
o: I, IV, V and VI only
I, II, III, V and VI only
II, III, IV and V only
I, II, III, IV and VI only
questions.e: Tobacco, Maize, Potato, Cashew Nut, and Pineapple were all introduced by Portuguese traders between the 16th and 17th centuries . Sugarcane, however, is indigenous to India.

questions.q: Q.39) In the context of medieval India, Darshani, Muddati and Jokhmi were:
questions.e: A Hundi was an indigenous financial instrument. Darshani was payable on sight, Muddati was a time bill/credit instrument, and Jokhmi was a conditional hundi for goods in transit (early insurance).

questions.q: Q.40) In the context of medieval India, consider the following statements: 1️⃣ Ahadis were peasants in the Mughal agrarian hierarchy. 2️⃣ Khud-kasht and Pahi-kasht were an elite class of troopers positioned between the ordinary soldiers and Mansabdars. 3️⃣ Gumashtas were agents of wholesale merchants who managed the complex logistics of trade. Which of the statements given above is/are not correct?
questions.e: Statements I and II are incorrect. Ahadis were elite gentlemen troopers. Khud-kasht and Pahi-kasht were categories of peasants (resident and non-resident) . Gumashtas were indeed agents for wholesale merchants.

questions.q: Q.41) How many of the following medieval saints were contemporaries of Akbar? 1️⃣ Sheikh Salim Chishti 2️⃣ Tulsidas 3️⃣ Dadu Dayal 4️⃣ Guru Nanak Dev
questions.e: Sheikh Salim Chishti (d. 1572), Tulsidas (1532–1623), and Dadu Dayal (1544–1603) were contemporaries of Akbar. Guru Nanak Dev (1469–1539) was a contemporary of Babur and Humayun.

questions.q: Q.42) Which of the following is the correct chronological order of the following battles? 1️⃣ Battle of Khanwa 2️⃣ Battle of Saraighat 3️⃣ Battle of Haldighati 4️⃣ Battle of Chausa
questions.e: The correct order is: Battle of Khanwa  , Battle of Chausa  , Battle of Haldighati  , and Battle of Saraighat .

questions.q: Q.43) With reference to the Akbar's revenue administration, consider the following statements: 1️⃣ In Batai, a rough estimate of the yield was made based on a visual inspection of the standing crop and past performance. 2️⃣ In Kankut, the actual produce was divided between the state and the peasant in a fixed proportion. 3️⃣ In Nasaq, a rough calculation was made based on past revenue receipts without new annual measurements. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement III is correct; Nasaq used past records without annual measurements. Statement I is incorrect because Batai was direct crop-sharing. Statement II is incorrect because Kankut was the method based on rough estimation and visual inspection of standing crops .

questions.q: Q.44) With reference to the reign of Jahangir, consider the following statements: 1️⃣ He faced a major revolt from Prince Khusrau leading to the Battle of Bhairowal. 2️⃣ He installed a golden chain of justice outside the Agra Fort allowing any subject to seek justice. 3️⃣ He gave trading permits to British officers Captain William Hawkins and Sir Thomas Roe.
questions.e: Jahangir defeated Prince Khusrau at the Battle of Bhairowal . He installed the golden chain of justice. While Sir Thomas Roe obtained a permit in 1615, Captain William Hawkins failed to secure one in 1608 .

questions.q: Q.45) Consider the following statements: 1️⃣ He forced the sultanates of Bijapur and Golconda to accept Mughal suzerainty. 2️⃣ He launched expeditions to conquer Balkh and Badakhshan, the ancestral lands of Mughals. 3️⃣ He established the chakla as a new administrative unit between the sarkar and the pargana. He was?
questions.e: Shah Jahan forced Bijapur and Golconda into suzerainty treaties. He launched the Central Asian campaign for Balkh and Badakhshan and introduced the 'chakla' as a new administrative unit.

questions.q: Q.46) Which one of the following battles is referred to in the description? 1️⃣ In this battle, a coalition of four Deccan Sultanates united against Vijayanagar. 2️⃣ After the battle, Tirumala Deva Raya moved the capital to Penukonda and later Chandragiri.
questions.e: The Battle of Talikota  involved a coalition of four Sultanates against Vijayanagar . After the defeat, Tirumala Deva Raya moved the capital to Penukonda and later Chandragiri.

questions.q: Q.47) How many of the following pairs regarding Vijayanagar water systems are correctly matched? 1️⃣ Reservoirs: Anicuts 2️⃣ Canals: Kere 3️⃣ Wells: Pushkarnis
questions.e: Only the third pair is correct; Pushkarnis were step wells. Anicuts were check dams built across riverbeds for canals , while Kere or sagara were vast reservoirs.

questions.q: Q.48) Which of the following is the correct chronological order of the dynasties who ruled the Vijayanagar empire?
questions.e: The dynasties ruled in this order: Sangama (1336–1485) , Saluva (1485–1505) , Tuluva (1505–1570) , and Aravidu (1570–1646).

questions.q: Q.49) In the context of the medieval India, Mahanavami Dibba was:
o: structure to conduct ceremonial events in the capital of the Vijayanagar Empire
central palace in Shivaji's kingdom where he was coronated
place where philosophical discussions among the medieval saints used to take place
questions.e: Mahanavami Dibba was a massive platform in the Vijayanagar Royal Center used for the 10-day Mahanavami festival. The King used it to witness festivities and military parades.

questions.q: Q.50) Consider the following statements: 1️⃣ Statement I: The collapse of the Vijayanagar central authority in the 16th century led to a severe and immediate decline in Portuguese maritime trade in the Indian Ocean. 2️⃣ Statement II: The destruction of the capital city, Hampi, and the subsequent fragmentation of the Vijayanagar empire halted the massive internal demand for luxury imports.
o: Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Both Statement I and Statement II are correct and Statement II is the correct explanation for Statement I
Both Statement I and Statement II are correct and Statement II is the correct explanation for Statement I
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
questions.e: Portuguese trade plummeted after 1565 because Vijayanagar was their largest consumer. The sacking of Hampi destroyed the concentrated demand for luxury imports like silk and velvet, and the collapse of the Rayas ended the high-revenue horse trade .

questions.q: Q.51) Consider the following statements: 1️⃣ Statement I: The "Tripartite Struggle" took place between the Pratiharas, the Palas and the Rashtrakutas for control over Kannauj. 2️⃣ Statement II: After the reign of Harshavardhana, Kannauj became the symbol of imperial status in northern India. 3️⃣ Statement III: Located in the fertile Gangetic Doab, Kannauj was a hub for trade and connected to the lucrative Silk Road.
o: Both Statement II and Statement III are correct but only one of them explains Statement I
Both Statement II and Statement III are correct and both of them explain Statement I
Neither Statement II nor Statement III is correct
Only one of the Statements II and III is correct and that explains Statement I
questions.e: The Tripartite Struggle involved the Gurjara-Pratiharas, Palas, and Rashtrakutas . Kannauj was a symbol of imperial sovereignty and strategically located in the fertile Gangetic Doab as a trade hub linked to the Silk Road. Thus, both statements explain the motivation for the conflict.

questions.q: Q.52) How many of the following pairs regarding Sufi Silsilas are correctly matched? 1️⃣ Chishti: Popularized Sama 2️⃣ Suhrawardi: Believed in living a life of poverty or seclusion 3️⃣ Naqshbandi: Practiced "silent dhikr" 4️⃣ Qadiri: Balanced approach between spiritual mysticism and orthodox practice
questions.e: Chishti, Naqshbandi, and Qadiri are correctly matched. Suhrawardis, unlike Chishtis, did not believe in poverty or seclusion; they accepted royal patronage and lived comfortable lives .

questions.q: Q.53) Which of the following dynasties were part of the Delhi Sultanate? 1️⃣ Slave Dynasty 2️⃣ Khalji Dynasty 3️⃣ Tughlaq Dynasty 4️⃣ Ghurid dynasty 5️⃣ Sayyid Dynasty 6️⃣ Lodi Dynasty
o: I, II, III, V and VI only
II, III, IV and V only
I, II, III, IV and VI only
I, IV, V and VI only
questions.e: The Delhi Sultanate (1206-1526) consisted of five dynasties: Slave, Khalji, Tughlaq, Sayyid, and Lodi . The Ghurid dynasty (1148-1215) preceded and established the foundation for the Sultanate but is not considered one of the five ruling dynasties of the Sultanate itself .

questions.q: Q.54) Consider the following statements with regard to Rajendra Chola I: 1️⃣ He assumed the title of Gangaikonda. 2️⃣ Ennayiram inscription states that he established a large Vedic college. 3️⃣ He maintained robust diplomatic ties with the Song Dynasty of China.
questions.e: Rajendra Chola I assumed the title 'Gangaikonda' after defeating the Pala king. His Ennayiram inscription records the establishment of a large Vedic college. He also maintained robust diplomatic and trade ties with the Song Dynasty.

questions.q: Q.55) How many of the following pairs regarding Pala and Pratihara administrative units are correctly matched? 1️⃣ Bhukti: Bhojapati 2️⃣ Mandala: Vishayapati 3️⃣ Pattala: Uparika
questions.e: Only Mandala-Vishayapati is correctly matched. Bhuktis (provinces) were governed by Uparikas. The unit below the district, called Pattala, was headed by a Bhojapati.

questions.q: Q.56) How many of the following were exported from India during the Delhi Sultanate? 1️⃣ Dry fruits 2️⃣ Sugar 3️⃣ Gold and silver 4️⃣ Muslins 5️⃣ Cloves
questions.e: Only sugar and muslins were exports. Dry fruits , cloves , and gold/silver  were primarily imports into India during the Delhi Sultanate.

questions.q: Q.57) How many of the following policies were initiated by Ala-ud-din Khalji? 1️⃣ Direct collection of land revenue 2️⃣ Regulation of market prices 3️⃣ Soldiers were paid through iqta grants
questions.e: Alauddin Khalji introduced direct collection of land revenue and a pioneering market price control system. However, he paid his soldiers in cash directly from the treasury, not through Iqta land grants.

questions.q: Q.58) Consider the following statements about Rajaraja Chola I: 1️⃣ He established a Chola province in northern Sri Lanka. 2️⃣ He built the Brihadeeswara temple at Gangaikonda Cholapuram. 3️⃣ He patronized the construction of the Chudamani Buddhist Vihara at Nagapattinam.
questions.e: Rajaraja I invaded northern Sri Lanka and established a province. He patronized the Chudamani Buddhist Vihara. However, he built the Brihadisvara Temple at Thanjavur, not Gangaikonda Cholapuram.

questions.q: Q.59) With reference to the Rashtrakutas, consider the following statements: 1️⃣ Govinda III made Sri Lanka a feudatory of the Rashtrakutas. 2️⃣ Amoghavarsha I authored Kavirajamarga, in the Kannada language. 3️⃣ Krishna III defeated the Cholas and built the Krishneswara temple at Rameshwaram.
questions.e: Govinda III obtained the submission of the King of Ceylon (Sri Lanka). Amoghavarsha I authored Kavirajamarga. Krishna III defeated the Cholas at the Battle of Takkolam and built the Krishneswara temple.

questions.q: Q.60) Consider the following statements about Vaishnava saint Ramananda: 1️⃣ He is best known for "bringing Bhakti from South India to North India". 2️⃣ He preached and composed in Sanskrit, making spiritual knowledge accessible to the common masses. 3️⃣ His approach is illustrated by his diverse group of the "Dwadash Mahant", Twelve Disciples.
questions.e: Ramananda is credited with bringing Bhakti to the North. He used Hindi, not Sanskrit, to make spiritual knowledge accessible. His inclusive approach is reflected in his 12 diverse disciples (Dwadash Mahant).

questions.q: Q.61) With reference to trade and commerce in early medieval India, consider the following statements: 1️⃣ Statement I: The early medieval times in India are marked by the scarcity of gold and silver coins. 2️⃣ Statement II: The Western Roman Empire declined in the 5th century CE. 3️⃣ Statement III: There was a rise of many regional states and the growth of localism in early medieval India.
o: Both Statement II and Statement III are correct but only one of them explains Statement I
Both Statement II and Statement III are correct and both of them explain Statement I
Only one of the Statements II and III is correct and that explains Statement I
Neither Statement II nor Statement III is correct
questions.e: Scarcity of coinage was driven by the decline of the Roman Empire (ending gold inflow) and the rise of internal localism and self-sufficiency within many regional states. Both external and internal factors explain the coinage paucity.

questions.q: Q.62) Which of the following statements is/are correct with regard to Firuz Tughlaq? 1️⃣ He reintroduced the system of hereditary appointments to offices. 2️⃣ He was the first Sultanate to have Hindu religious works translated from Sanskrit to Persian. 3️⃣ He imposed an irrigation tax to fund canal projects.
questions.e: Firuz Tughlaq reintroduced hereditary appointments. He was the first to translate Hindu religious works from Sanskrit to Persian. He undertook irrigation projects and introduced 'Haq-i-Sharb' (10% irrigation tax).

questions.q: Q.63) Which of the following battles laid the foundation of Turkish rule in north India? 1️⃣ Battle of Waihind, 1009 AD 2️⃣ Battle of Mahoba, 1183 AD 3️⃣ Battles of Tarain, 1192 AD 4️⃣ Battle of Chandawar, 1194 AD
questions.e: The Second Battle of Tarain  was the turning point that established Turkish bases. The Battle of Chandawar  established control over the Gangetic plains. Waihind and Mahoba were earlier conflicts.

questions.q: Q.64) Consider the following statements about the Arab merchant, Sulaiman: 1️⃣ His account Akhbar al-Sind wa'l-Hind is among the earliest foreign descriptions of medieval India. 2️⃣ He ranked the Rashtrakuta King Amoghavarsha I among the four greatest kings of the world.
questions.e: Sulaiman's 'Akhbar al-Sind wa'l-Hind' (851 CE) is one of the earliest reliable foreign descriptions. He ranked the Rashtrakuta King (Amoghavarsha I) among the four greatest kings of the world .

questions.q: Q.65) How many of the following rows regarding Rajput Kingdoms are correctly matched? 1️⃣ Tomaras: Haryana, Founded Delhi 2️⃣ Solankis: Gujarat, Defeated Ghori at Kasahrada 3️⃣ Paramaras: Bundelkhand, Raja Bhoja 4️⃣ Chandelas: Malwa, Khajuraho
questions.e: Tomaras and Solankis are correctly matched . The Paramaras ruled Malwa (not Bundelkhand) , and the Chandelas ruled Bundelkhand (not Malwa) and built Khajuraho .

questions.q: Q.66) Which of the following statements is/are correct with reference to the military reforms in Delhi Sultanate? 1️⃣ For the first time, a specialized military department was established. 2️⃣ Horses were branded and a detailed descriptive roll was given for every soldier. 3️⃣ The military strength was built upon heavy cavalry and mechanical artillery.
questions.e: Balban established the Diwan-i-Arz military department. Alauddin Khalji introduced branding of horses (Dagh) and descriptive rolls (Chehra). The army shifted to Turkish cavalry and used mechanical artillery like catapults .

questions.q: Q.67) Which of the following statements is not correct with reference to the Bhakti saint Vallabhacharya? 1️⃣ He is most celebrated for founding the Pushtimarg or the Path of Grace. 2️⃣ He propounded the Vedantic philosophy of Shuddhadvaita or Pure Non-Dualism. 3️⃣ He authored Sanskrit texts, the Anubhashya and the Subodhini.
questions.e: All statements provided in the question text are actually correct. Vallabhacharya founded Pushtimarg , propounded Shuddhadvaita , and authored the Anubhashya and Subodhini.

questions.q: Q.68) Which of the following statements is not correct with reference to the Imperial Cholas?
o: The Cholas undertook extensive land surveys and revenue settlements.
Vativaykkal was a traditional way of harnessing rain water in the Kavery delta.
Vetti and amanji were forms of forced labour at the village level.
The Chola state collected land tax out of the agrarian surplus for its revenue.
questions.e: Statement (d) is incorrect because vetti and amanji were forms of free labour for public works, not necessarily forced/bonded labour in the modern sense. Cholas did undertake surveys , collected land tax , and used the vativaykkal channel system.

questions.q: Q.69) Consider the following statements about the 14th century traveler Ibn Battuta: 1️⃣ Muhammad bin Tughlaq appointed Ibn Battuta as the Chief Qazi (judge) of Delhi. 2️⃣ His travelogue Rihla, documented a wide array of social customs of the time.
questions.e: Ibn Battuta was appointed Chief Qazi of Delhi by Muhammad bin Tughlaq. His travelogue, 'The Rihla', provides detailed insights into social customs, the postal system, and political policies.

questions.q: Q.70) With reference to the Sufi orders, consider the following statements: 1️⃣ Ba-shara sufis were not bound by the religious rituals and often led a life of extreme asceticism and solitude. 2️⃣ Be-shara sufis followed the formal Islamic laws and maintained an organized lineages of succession.
questions.e: Both statements are swapped. Ba-shara Sufis followed Sharia (Islamic law) and maintained organized lineages. Be-shara Sufis did not feel bound by Sharia and often led lives of extreme asceticism .

questions.q: Q.71) Consider the following statements about the Bhakti saint-poet, Namdev: 1️⃣ He belonged to the Shaiva tradition. 2️⃣ He transitioned from the Saguna to the Nirguna Bhakti. 3️⃣ He composed devotional poems called Abhangas.
questions.e: Namdev was a key figure in the Varkari tradition, which worships Lord Vitthal (Vishnu/Krishna), so he belonged to the Vaishnava, not Shaiva, tradition . He transitioned from Saguna to Nirguna Bhakti and composed Abhangas.

questions.q: Q.72) With reference to the Uttaramerur inscription, consider the following statements: 1️⃣ It laid down a detailed "constitution" for local self-government in the Pandya kingdom. 2️⃣ Representatives to village assembly were selected through a system known as Kudavolai. 3️⃣ Age, property and the knowledge of the Vedas were the qualification criteria for the candidates.
questions.e: Statement I is incorrect because the Uttaramerur inscription belongs to the Chola Empire (reign of Parantaka I), not the Pandya kingdom. The system used was Kudavolai , and candidates had criteria for age, property, and Vedic knowledge .

questions.q: Q.73) How many of the following statements regarding trade between India and Southeast Asia in the early medieval period are correct? 1️⃣ The chief port for sailing to Java and Sumatra was Tamralipti in Bengal. 2️⃣ Trade relations led to the "Indianization" of Southeast Asia. 3️⃣ Harisena's Brihatkathakosh discusses the growing proximity between the two regions.
questions.e: Tamralipti was the chief port for Southeast Asian trade. This era saw the "Indianization" of the region through merchants and priests. Books like 'Brihatkathakosh' reflect the growing proximity .

questions.q: Q.74) Consider the following statements about Guru Nanak Dev: 1️⃣ He laid great emphasis on the one God by repeating whose name one could get salvation. 2️⃣ He advocated a life of ascetic and living in solitude. 3️⃣ He sang his hymns to the accompaniment of the rabaab instrument.
questions.e: Guru Nanak emphasized one God and salvation through his name. He used the rabaab instrument for his hymns. However, he did not advocate asceticism; he promoted a middle path combining spiritual life with householder duties .

questions.q: Q.75) Consider the following statements: 1️⃣ He expounded the Vedantic philosophy Achintya Bheda Abheda. 2️⃣ He popularized the mass chanting of the Hare Krishna Maha-mantra. 3️⃣ Shikshashtakam is the only written record of his personal teachings. 4️⃣ He is credited with rediscovering and revitalizing Vrindavan as a major pilgrimage center. Who was he?
questions.e: Chaitanya Mahaprabhu expounded Achintya Bheda Abheda and popularized the Hare Krishna Maha-mantra. His only written record is the Shikshashtakam , and he revitalized Vrindavan.

questions.q: Q.76) How many of the following developments were introduced in India during the Delhi Sultanate? 1️⃣ Paper-making and bookbinding 2️⃣ Use of gunpowder 3️⃣ Spinning Wheel 4️⃣ Telescope 5️⃣ Sericulture 6️⃣ Lime mortar and gypsum as binding materials 7️⃣ Use of Rahat in agriculture
o: I, IV, V and VI only
I, II, III, IV, V and VI only
II, III, IV, and VII only
I, II, III, V, VI and VII only
questions.e: All developments listed were introduced during the Delhi Sultanate except the telescope, which was introduced later during the Mughal era .

questions.q: Q.77) Which of the following statements with reference to the Alvars are correct? 1️⃣ They were Tamil poet-saints of South India devoted to the worship of Lord Shiva. 2️⃣ Their devotional hymns were compiled by Nathamuni as Naalayira Divya Prabandham. 3️⃣ Andal was the only female saint among the Alvars.
questions.e: Statement I is incorrect; Alvars were devoted to Lord Vishnu. Nayanars were devoted to Lord Shiva. Nathamuni compiled the Alvars' hymns , and Andal was the only female among the 12 Alvars.

questions.q: Q.78) Which of the following is the correct hierarchical order of the officials from higher to lower in the administration of the Delhi Sultanate?
questions.e: The provincial head was the Wali/Muqti. The Shiqdar headed the Shiq (district). The Amil was at the Pargana level , and the Chaudhari was a village-level official.

questions.q: Q.79) Consider the following statements regarding a medieval figure: 1️⃣ For him, liberation from the cycle of birth and death is achieved through Jnana or self-realization. 2️⃣ He established four monastic centers each associated with one of the four Vedas. 3️⃣ His legacy is honored by the 108-foot "Statue of Oneness" in Omkareshwar, Madhya Pradesh. Who among the following is best described?
questions.e: Adi Shankara taught that liberation is through Jnana. He established four mathas (Sringeri, Dwaraka, Puri, Joshimath). The "Statue of Oneness" in Omkareshwar honors him .

questions.q: Q.80) How many of the following statements regarding Chola local administration are correct? 1️⃣ Urar consisted of landholders and tax-paying residents of the village. 2️⃣ Sabhaiyar was the assembly found in Brahmadeya villages. 3️⃣ Nagarattar administered specialized settlements of traders and skilled artisans. 4️⃣ Nattar served as the assembly of eminent landholders from the villages within the Nadu.
questions.e: All four are correct: Urar for non-Brahmin villages , Sabhaiyar for Brahmadeya villages , Nagarattar for urban/trader centers , and Nattar for the Nadu unit.

questions.q: Q.81) How many of the following statements regarding Al-Biruni are not correct? 1️⃣ He came to India along with Babur. 2️⃣ His work Kitab-ul-Hind is a systematic study of India. 3️⃣ He transmitted Aryabhata's work Aryabattiya to the West.
questions.e: Only Statement I is incorrect; Al-Biruni came to India with Mahmud of Ghazni, not Babur . His work 'Kitab-ul-Hind' is a systematic study , and he transmitted Aryabhata's work to the West.

questions.q: Q.82) With reference to the Slave dynasty, consider the following statements: 1️⃣ Muhammad Ghori was the founder of the Delhi Sultanate and the first ruler of the Slave Dynasty. 2️⃣ Iltutmish created the Chahalgani system, an elite group of 40 loyal Turkish slave-officers.
questions.e: Qutb-ud-din Aibak (a slave of Ghori), not Ghori himself, was the founder of the Delhi Sultanate and first Slave ruler . Iltutmish did create the Turkan-i-Chahalgani (Corps of Forty).

questions.q: Q.83) In the context of early medieval India, nad-gavundas and desa-gramakutas were:
questions.e: In the Rashtrakuta Empire, nad-gavundas and desa-gramakutas were hereditary revenue officers responsible for managing the countryside .

questions.q: Q.84) How many of the following statements regarding administrative initiatives by Muhammad Bin Tughlaq are not correct? 1️⃣ He shifted the capital from Delhi to Devagiri in Deccan and named it Daulatabad. 2️⃣ He introduced copper and brass coins as token currency, declaring them equal in value to silver tankas. 3️⃣ He created a dedicated Department of Agriculture called Diwan-i-Amir-i-Kohi.
questions.e: All statements are actually correct. He shifted the capital to Daulatabad , introduced token currency , and created the agriculture department Diwan-i-Amir-i-Kohi.

questions.q: Q.85) How many of the following statements regarding bhakti saint Kabir are correct? 1️⃣ He advocated for the worship of a formless, universal Divine or Nirguna Brahman. 2️⃣ The 'Bijak' is the compilation of his verses. 3️⃣ The Guru Granth Sahib contains more than 500 hymns composed by Kabir.
questions.e: Kabir advocated Nirguna Bhakti. The 'Bijak' is the primary compilation of his verses. The Guru Granth Sahib contains over 540 of his hymns.

questions.q: Q.86) Consider the following statements: 1️⃣ Statement I: The Delhi Sultanate was formally considered to be an Islamic State. 2️⃣ Statement II: Most Delhi Sultans sought formal recognition from the Abbasid Caliph in Baghdad. 3️⃣ Statement III: The Sultans of Delhi generally prioritized strict Sharia (religious law) over Zawabit (state laws).
o: Neither Statement II nor Statement III is correct
Both Statement II and Statement III are correct but only one of them explains Statement I
Both Statement II and Statement III are correct and both of them explain Statement I
Only one of the Statements II and III is correct and that explains Statement I
questions.e: Statement III is incorrect; Sultans used state laws (Zawabit) and often separated religion from politics for state welfare. Most did seek formal recognition from the Caliph to provide religious and legal legitimacy (Statement II).

questions.q: Q.87) Consider the following statements: 1️⃣ Statement I: The establishment of the Delhi Sultanate ushered a new phase of urban growth. 2️⃣ Statement II: A higher degree of monetization in the rural economy was seen during Delhi Sultanate rule.
o: Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Both Statement I and Statement II are correct and Statement II explains Statement I
Both Statement I and Statement II are correct but Statement II does not explain Statement I
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
questions.e: The Sultanate's demand for cash taxes forced monetization in the rural economy as peasants sold surplus in towns, thereby drawing products to cities and fueling urban growth .

questions.q: Q.88) With reference to the administration of Rashtrakutas, consider the following statements: 1️⃣ Rashtra was the largest unit of administration under the control of the Vishayapati. 2️⃣ Prabhu Gavunda was village headman responsible for local security and revenue.
questions.e: A Rashtra (province) was headed by a Rashtrapati . The Vishayapati headed a Vishaya (district). The village headman was the Prabhu Gavunda (or Gramapala).

questions.q: Q.89) How many of the following pairs regarding Delhi Sultanate departments are correctly matched? 1️⃣ Diwan-i-Wizarat: Finance 2️⃣ Diwan-i-Arz: Religious Affairs 3️⃣ Diwan-i-Insha: Correspondence 4️⃣ Diwan-i-Risalat: Discipline of royal army
questions.e: Only Wizarat (Finance) and Insha (Correspondence) are correctly matched. Diwan-i-Arz was the Military department , and Diwan-i-Risalat was the department for Religious Affairs/Judiciary .

questions.q: Q.90) Which of the statements given above regarding Nayanars are not correct? 1️⃣ Their devotional hymns were compiled into a 12-volume series called the Tirumurai. 2️⃣ The epic Periya Puranam contains the details of the Nayanar saints.
questions.e: Both statements are correct. Nayanars' hymns are in the 12-volume 'Tirumurai' , and 'Periya Puranam' provides details of the 63 saints .

questions.q: Q.91) How many of the following pairs regarding urban specialization are correctly matched? 1️⃣ Sonargaon: Fine muslins 2️⃣ Cambay: Indigo 3️⃣ Bayana: Gold and silver work 4️⃣ Kashmir: Carpet weaving
questions.e: Sonargaon (muslins) and Kashmir (carpet weaving) are correct. Cambay was known for cotton, silk, and gold work , while Bayana (and Lahore) were famous for indigo.

questions.q: Q.92) With reference to the Vishishtadvaita philosophy, consider the following statements: 1️⃣ It asserts that while the Ultimate Reality is one, it is "qualified" by internal differences. 2️⃣ It was systematically developed by the 11th-century philosopher-saint Ramanuja.
questions.e: Vishishtadvaita means "Qualified Non-Dualism," asserting the Ultimate Reality is one but qualified by differences. It was developed by Ramanuja in the 11th century.

questions.q: Q.93) How many of the following statements regarding the Virashaiva movement are correct? 1️⃣ It originated in the 12th century socio-religious reform movement led by Basavanna. 2️⃣ Anubhava Mantapa was a democratic parliament where people discussed philosophy. 3️⃣ The philosophy of the movement was recorded in Vachanas.
questions.e: The movement was led by Basavanna in the 12th century. He established the Anubhava Mantapa as a democratic parliament. The philosophy was recorded in simple Kannada poems called Vachanas.

questions.q: Q.94) How many of the following pairs regarding Delhi Sultanate land types are correctly matched? 1️⃣ Khalisa: Land assigned to military officials in lieu of a cash salary 2️⃣ Iqta: Land directly managed by the central government 3️⃣ Waqf: Land grants given to religious institutions
questions.e: Only Waqf is correct . Khalisa land was directly managed by the central government. Iqta was land assigned to military officials in lieu of salary.

questions.q: Q.95) Minhaj-i-Siraj Juzjani's Tabaqat-i-Nasiri as the most authoritative source of:
o: the establishment of the Mughal rule
religion and customs during medieval times
decline of Southern kingdoms during early medieval times
questions.e: 'Tabaqat-i-Nasiri' is the most authoritative Persian source for the foundation of the Delhi Sultanate (specifically the Ghurid and Slave dynasties), not Mughal rule or southern kingdoms .

questions.q: Q.96) With reference to the Pratihara Empire, consider the following statements: 1️⃣ At its zenith, it stretched from the border of Sindh in the west to Bengal in the east. 2️⃣ Umayyad Caliphate's military campaigns in the 8th century weekend the empire. 3️⃣ The Sanskrit poet and dramatist Rajashekhara lived at the court of Mahipala I.
questions.e: The Pratihara Empire stretched from Sindh to Bengal at its peak. Rajashekhara lived at the court of Mahendrapala I and Mahipala I. However, the 8th-century Umayyad campaigns were successfully repelled by Nagabhata I, rather than weakening the empire.

questions.q: Q.97) He was a versatile poet, musician, scholar, and mystic who had a profound and lasting impact on the cultural history of the Indian subcontinent during the Delhi Sultanate. He is widely credited with developing Hindavi which laid the foundation for modern Hindi and Urdu. He authored Tughlaq Nama. He was also a devoted disciple of the Nizamuddin Auliya. He was:
questions.e: Amir Khusrau (Tuti-yi-Hind) developed Hindavi, served multiple rulers, authored the 'Tughlaq Nama', and was a disciple of Nizamuddin Auliya .

questions.q: Q.98) With reference to the Siddhas, consider the following statements: 1️⃣ They advocated for a personal experience of the divine (Sivam) through inner discipline. 2️⃣ Tirumular's Thirumandiram is a Sidhha text. 3️⃣ They founded Varma Kalai, a martial art focusing on vital pressure points.
questions.e: Siddhars (Sittars) advocated for personal experience of the divine (Civam) . Tirumular's 'Thirumandiram' is a major medieval Siddha text. They also founded Varma Kalai.

questions.q: Q.99) With reference to the Imperial Cholas, consider the following statements: 1️⃣ Their rule was established by Vijayalaya with Thanjavur as its capital. 2️⃣ They controlled both the Coromandel and Malabar coasts. 3️⃣ Meikeertis were the detailed historical records written on the walls of their temples.
questions.e: Vijayalaya established the Chola kingdom with Thanjavur as capital . They controlled both the Coromandel and Malabar coasts. They used Meikeertis (historical records) on temple walls.

questions.q: Q.100) Ziauddin Barani, the chronicler of the Delhi Sultanate, was a contemporary of the:
questions.e: Ziauddin Barani was a contemporary of Muhammad bin Tughlaq and Firuz Shah Tughlaq. His 'Tarikh-i-Firoz Shahi' covers history up to the sixth year of Firuz Shah Tughlaq.

questions.q: Q.1) A favourable balance of trade is indicated by which one of the following?
o: Export receipts and import payments are equal, and capital inflows match capital outflows over a financial year
A country earns more from selling goods abroad than it spends on buying goods from abroad
The value of imports consistently surpasses the value of exports, but is offset by large inflows of Foreign Direct Investment
A country deliberately boosts imports and restricts capital outflows to strengthen domestic competition and innovation
questions.e: The balance of trade is the difference between export receipts and import payments. Trade balance equals Export minus Import. If the balance is positive (earning more from exports than spending on imports), it is called a favourable balance of trade.

questions.q: Q.2) Which of the following are considered "Invisibles" under Current Account transactions? — 1️⃣ IT-Enabled Services (ITES) 2️⃣ Grants 3️⃣ Maintenance of embassies and diplomatic missions 4️⃣ Interest from loans
questions.e: Current account invisibles record receipts and payments for services, transfers, and income. Services include software services (IT/ITES) and government Not Included Elsewhere, such as maintenance of embassies. Transfers include grants and gifts. Income includes interest from loans, dividends, and profit.

questions.q: Q.3) Consider the following — 1️⃣ Royalties 2️⃣ Dividends from investments 3️⃣ Remittances 4️⃣ Multilateral loans
questions.e: Multilateral loans (official transactions with bodies like the World Bank/IMF) are part of the Capital Account. However, royalties, dividends from investments, and remittances are classified as Current Account transactions.

questions.q: Q.4) Other things remaining unchanged, a rise in the price of foreign exchange will lead to — 1️⃣ increase in exports from India 2️⃣ increase in Foreign Direct investment (FDI) in India 3️⃣ increase in foreigner's costs while purchasing products from India 4️⃣ increase in the supply of foreign currency
questions.e: A rise in the price of foreign exchange (depreciation of domestic currency) makes exports cheaper, increasing India's exports. FDI increases because more investment can be made with the same amount of dollars. Foreigners' costs actually reduce as more products can be bought with an appreciated dollar. Increased exports lead to an increased supply of foreign exchange, showing a positive relationship.

questions.q: Q.5) The foreign exchange reserves of the Reserve Bank of India consist of — 1️⃣ Foreign Currency Assets 2️⃣ Green deposits 3️⃣ Special Drawing Right (SDR) holdings of the government 4️⃣ Reserve Tranche
questions.e: Foreign exchange reserves include Foreign Currency Assets, Gold stock of the RBI, Special Drawing Right (SDR) holdings, and the Reserve Tranche. Green deposits are excluded because the current framework permits them to be denominated in Indian Rupees only.

questions.q: Q.6) Statement I: Devaluation is a policy action whereby a government officially reduces the value of its currency. Statement II: Devaluation of currency is undertaken to boost its exports in the international market.
o: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct and Statement II explains Statement I
Both Statement I and Statement II are correct but Statement II does not explain Statement I
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
questions.e: Devaluation is the reduction in the external value of the home currency. It is aimed at increasing a country's exports by making them cheaper for foreign buyers. It is usually resorted to to correct a deficit in the balance of trade.

questions.q: Q.7) An Indian who was earlier a resident but later migrated abroad opens a Non-Resident Ordinary (NRO) Account in India. Which of the following is correct regarding this account?
o: It cannot be used as a fixed deposit account.
It allows free repatriation of all foreign income without restrictions.
Its interest rate is linked to the LIBOR/SWAP rate.
It is held in Indian Rupees.
questions.e: An NRO account is held by Indians ordinarily living abroad and is maintained in Indian Rupees. It can be opened as current, savings, recurring, or fixed deposit accounts. Unlike FCNR(B) or NRE accounts, its interest is not specifically noted as pegged to LIBOR/SWAP in the same way.

questions.q: Q.8) In India, the end-use restriction on External Commercial Borrowings (ECBs) is applicable to which of the following cases? — 1️⃣ Leasing property for buying 2️⃣ Investment in the capital market 3️⃣ Equity investments 4️⃣ Foreign Currency Convertible Bonds listed on the National Stock Exchange
questions.e: ECBs have a negative list for which loans cannot be made (end-use restrictions). This includes real estate activities like owning or leasing property for buying/selling , investments in capital markets , and equity investments. FCCBs listed on BSE/NSE are part of the eligibility/approval criteria rather than the restricted end-use list.

questions.q: Q.9) The term "paper gold" refers to:
o: Gold reserves held in dematerialized form by the central bank
Special Drawing Rights (SDR) holdings of the government
Government securities issued against gold deposits
Gold-backed exchange-traded funds held by investors
questions.e: Special Drawing Rights (SDR) are known as "paper gold". It is an international reserve asset created by the IMF in 1969. While it is not a currency itself, it represents a potential claim on the freely usable currencies of IMF members.

questions.q: Q.10) The effect of rupee depreciation in India is that it generally — 1️⃣ increases the exports 2️⃣ increases the aggregate demand for domestically produced goods 3️⃣ increases the rate of inflation in India
questions.e: Currency depreciation makes goods cheaper for foreigners, raising exports. It makes imports more expensive, leading people to substitute them with domestically produced goods, thus increasing net aggregate demand. However, costlier imports (like oil) push up domestic inflation and widen the trade deficit.

questions.q: Q.11) In the context of capital accounts, which of the following are considered Foreign assets of commercial banks? — 1️⃣ Foreign currency holdings 2️⃣ Rupee overdrafts to non-resident banks 3️⃣ Non-resident deposits
questions.e: Foreign assets of commercial banks include foreign currency holdings and rupee overdrafts to non-resident banks. Non-resident deposits are classified as "Foreign liabilities" of commercial banks.

questions.q: Q.12) Which one of the following statements best describes the term 'Import Coverage Ratio'?
o: Share of a country's own imports that is subject to a particular non-tariff barrier
Value of a country's foreign reserves sufficient to cover 15 months' worth of essential imports
Volume of imported intermediate goods that are exported after processing into final goods
Ratio of the value of exported goods and services to imported goods and services
questions.e: An Import Coverage Ratio is the share or percentage of a country's own imports that is subject to a particular non-tariff barrier or a group of such barriers. It is calculated using actual values of bilateral trade flows.

questions.q: Q.13) Statement I: The PPP-based exchange rate is preferred over the market-based exchange rate to compare the standard of living of people. Statement II: The PPP-based exchange rate does not reflect the purchasing power of money to buy non-traded goods.
o: Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are correct but Statement II does not explain Statement I
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Both Statement I and Statement II are correct and Statement II explains Statement I
questions.e: PPP-based exchange rates are used to compare the standard of living and stages of development. Statement II is incorrect because it is actually the market-based (trade-based) exchange rate that fails to reflect the purchasing power for non-traded goods, whereas PPP is designed to account for these differences.

questions.q: Q.14) "Duties are the types of indirect taxes levied on goods and services. Duties on domestic goods are called (blank) while, when levied on imports, are called (blank). (blank) is a tax imposed on imported goods majorly to protect the domestic producers."
questions.e: Duties on goods manufactured domestically are known as excise duties. Indirect taxes imposed on consumers who import goods are customs duties. A tariff is a tax imposed by the government on imported goods specifically to protect domestic producers and discourage imports.

questions.q: Q.15) Which one of the following is the most likely impact of the increased consumer income on the Indian Rupee?
o: Depreciation of the Indian rupee will be twice of the increase in income
Indian rupee may or may not depreciate
questions.e: Increased income increases spending on imports, which shifts the demand curve for foreign exchange and can lead to depreciation. However, if income abroad also increases, exports rise, shifting the supply curve. Therefore, on balance, the domestic currency may or may not depreciate depending on which factor is stronger.

questions.q: Q.16) Consider the following rows — 1️⃣ Preferential Trade Agreement (PTA): The level of tariff is reduced among parties - Example: CETA 2️⃣ Customs Union (CU): Parties generally adopt a common currency - Example: MERCOSUR 3️⃣ Common Market (CM): Allows free movement of labour, capital, and services - Example: European Union 4️⃣ Free Trade Agreement (FTA): The level of tariff is completely removed - Example: SAFTA
questions.e: Row I is correct; PTAs like CETA reduce tariffs. Row III is correct; Common Markets like MERCOSUR allow free movement of goods, services, capital, and people. Row II is incorrect; Customs Unions maintain a common external tariff, not necessarily a common currency (which is a feature of an EMU). Row IV is incorrect; SAFTA is an FTA, but the description provided for FTA is incomplete or mismatched compared to the EMU example for EU.

questions.q: Q.17) In which of the following scenarios is trade between two countries most likely to be mutually beneficial?
o: Both countries export goods in which they have a comparative advantage
Both countries export goods in which they have high absolute productivity, even if opportunity costs are identical
Both countries export the same goods with similar production costs
questions.e: Comparative advantage theory suggests a country should produce and export goods in which it has a comparative advantage (lower opportunity cost). Specialized trade based on this allows both countries to receive more in return than they could produce internally.

questions.q: Q.18) With reference to the Full Capital Account Convertibility in India, consider the following — 1️⃣ It refers to the freedom to convert local financial assets into foreign financial assets and vice versa. 2️⃣ It helps Indian companies to get External Commercial Borrowings (ECBs) without the approval of the Reserve Bank of India. 3️⃣ The S.S. Tarapore Committee recommended bringing the fiscal deficit down to 2% of GDP to ensure economic stability before moving towards full capital account convertibility.
questions.e: Capital Account Convertibility is defined as the freedom to convert local financial assets into foreign ones and vice versa. It allows companies to obtain ECBs without RBI approval. However, the Tarapore Committee recommended a fiscal deficit of 3.5%, not 2%.

questions.q: Q.19) Which of the following statements is/are correct with regard to NEER and REER? — 1️⃣ The REER is the weighted average of a country's currency in relation to an index or basket of other major currencies. 2️⃣ A decrease in the NEER suggests that exports become cheaper and imports become more expensive, enhancing trade competitiveness.
questions.e: Statement I is incorrect; NEER is the weighted average in relation to a basket of currencies , while REER is that same average adjusted for inflation. Statement II is correct; a decrease in NEER means exports become cheaper and imports more expensive, enhancing competitiveness.

questions.q: Q.20) A country runs a persistent trade deficit, yet economists suggest that it may reflect rising growth prospects rather than economic weakness. Which of the following best explains this view?
o: A trade deficit ensures that the domestic currency will appreciate in the long run, boosting foreign investment
A trade deficit prevents access to international savings and limits investment-led growth
A trade deficit always indicates that domestic industries are becoming less competitive in global markets
A trade deficit can help bring foreign investment, financing higher levels of domestic investment than what national savings alone can support
questions.e: A trade deficit can signal strong growth if it occurs because foreign investors are supplying capital to fund domestic investment. This inflow of foreign capital, if invested wisely, increases productivity and expands production capacity.

questions.q: Q.21) Which of the following statements are correct with regard to the internationalisation of the rupee? — 1️⃣ It can help mitigate currency risks for Indian businesses. 2️⃣ It will require India to hold large foreign exchange reserves. 3️⃣ It can increase the bargaining power of Indian businesses in international trade. 4️⃣ It can make India more vulnerable to external economic shocks.
questions.e: Internationalisation reduces currency risk for businesses and increases their bargaining power. However, it actually reduces the need for large foreign exchange reserves and aims to make India less vulnerable to external shocks by reducing reliance on foreign currencies.

questions.q: Q.22) With reference to Interest Rate Differential (IRD), consider the following — 1️⃣ It is the difference between the interest rate and the GDP growth rate of an economy. 2️⃣ An increase in interest rates at home leads to an appreciation of the domestic currency. 3️⃣ Among all types of capital flows, Foreign Direct Investment (FDI) is most affected by IRD.
questions.e: IRD is the difference between interest rates between countries, not GDP growth. Higher domestic interest rates attract investors, reducing demand for foreign currency and leading to appreciation. FDI is actually the least likely to be influenced by IRD because it is long-term and involves taking a stake in a company.

questions.q: Q.23) Consider the following pairs — 1️⃣ Crawling Peg: Exchange rate is determined purely by market forces 2️⃣ Dirty Floating: Central Bank occasionally intervenes to reduce excessive volatility 3️⃣ Adjusted Peg: Central bank can adjust the rate periodically
questions.e: Pair II is correct; in a Dirty Floating system, the central bank intervenes to smooth fluctuations. Pair III is correct; an Adjusted Peg allows the rate to be adjusted periodically. Pair I is incorrect; in a Crawling Peg, the bank makes small adjustments, whereas market forces purely determine the rate in a "Clean Floating" system.

questions.q: Q.24) Consider the following — 1️⃣ Fixing a limit on the quantity of tradable goods 2️⃣ Granting production subsidies to producers of exportable goods 3️⃣ Fixing standards of goods packaging
questions.e: Non-tariff barriers include Quotas (fixing quantity limits) , production subsidies (low-cost raw materials/tax concessions) , and packaging requirements which push up product costs.

questions.q: Q.25) Consider the following events — 1️⃣ Increase in the global oil prices 2️⃣ Increase in India's Current Account Deficit 3️⃣ Depreciation of Indian currency against other currencies
questions.e: High oil prices increase revenues in oil-producing countries, increasing demand for migrant workers and inward remittances to India. Currency depreciation also has a positive impact because remitters get better value in rupee terms. However, a higher CAD is a result of import/export imbalances; remittances actually help narrow or offset the CAD rather than being caused by its increase.

questions.q: Q.26) Which one of the following statements is correct with reference to the 'Impossible Trinity' in economics?
o: A Central Bank cannot maintain a fixed foreign exchange rate and low inflation at the same time.
It is not possible to maintain the goals of free capital flows, fixed-exchange-rate and an independent monetary policy at the same time.
A country cannot have domestic currency appreciation and a low current account deficit at the same time.
It states that a country cannot maintain the goal of free capital flows, a stable financial market and low inflation at the same time.
questions.e: The Impossible Trinity theory states that a country cannot simultaneously maintain free capital flows, a fixed exchange rate, and an independent monetary policy. A Central Bank must choose between a fixed rate and capital mobility if it wants an independent policy.

questions.q: Q.27) With reference to Currency Swap Agreement, consider the following — 1️⃣ It allows countries to pay for imports and exports at pre-determined exchange rates. 2️⃣ It reduces the need of maintaining foreign exchange reserves for bilateral trade 3️⃣ It is used to counter volatile exchange rates or market risks.
questions.e: Currency swaps involve trade in local currencies at pre-determined rates. They address short-term liquidity mismatches and reduce the need for foreign exchange reserves in bilateral trade. They also carry no exchange rate risk as terms are set in advance, hedging against volatility.

questions.q: Q.28) With reference to the World Trade Organisation (WTO), consider the following pairs — 1️⃣ Amber Box: It includes domestic support measures which do not distort trade 2️⃣ Green Box: It includes subsidies that distort trade, and are thus subject to limitations 3️⃣ Blue Box: It includes support measures that require farmers to limit production
questions.e: Pair III is correctly matched; Blue Box subsidies are "amber box with conditions" requiring farmers to limit production. Pair I and II are swapped; Amber Box includes measures that distort trade , while Green Box includes subsidies that cause minimal or no trade distortion.

questions.q: Q.29) Which of the following trade practices is/are prohibited under World Trade Organization (WTO) mandates? — 1️⃣ Domestic content requirement 2️⃣ Local employment requirement 3️⃣ Rules of origin
questions.e: Domestic content requirements are explicitly prohibited under the TRIMs agreement as they violate national treatment. Local employment requirements are not explicitly prohibited in all cases but may implicitly violate norms. Rules of origin are not prohibited; the WTO actually encourages their harmonization.

questions.q: Q.30) Statement I: Non-traded goods and services tend to be cheaper in low-income countries than high income countries. Statement II: Low-income countries tend to have weaker currencies compared to high-income countries.
o: Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Both Statement I and Statement II are correct but Statement II does not explain Statement I
Both Statement I and Statement II are correct and Statement II explains Statement I
questions.e: Non-traded goods are cheaper in low-income countries due to lower labor and living costs. Low-income countries also tend to have weaker currencies due to inflation or lower reserves. However, currency weakness (Statement II) primarily affects traded goods and does not necessarily explain the lower cost of non-traded goods (Statement I).

questions.q: Q.31) Consider the following pairs — 1️⃣ Anti-dumping duty: Imposed when a country is paying the subsidy to its exporters 2️⃣ Countervailing Duty: Imposed on imported goods to equalize imports with local taxes 3️⃣ Safeguard measures: Imposed on imports manufactured in foreign countries priced below the fair market value
questions.e: All three pairs are mismatched. Anti-dumping duty is for goods priced below fair market value. Countervailing Duty is imposed when a foreign country provides subsidies to its exporters. Safeguard measures are for unexpectedly increasing imports that threaten domestic industry. Equalizing imports with local taxes is the role of Additional Customs Duty.

questions.q: Q.32) Statement I: A surplus Balance of Payments (BoP) may lead to an appreciation of the domestic currency. Statement II: A surplus BoP results in an increased demand for the country's currency.
o: Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Both Statement I and Statement II are correct and Statement II explains Statement I
Both Statement I and Statement II are correct but Statement II does not explain Statement I
questions.e: A BoP surplus means a country receives more foreign currency than it spends, which typically strengthens the domestic currency. This occurs because foreign buyers need to convert their currency into the domestic one, increasing demand and causing appreciation.

questions.q: Q.33) Which of the following statements best describes the concept of 'parallel imports'?
o: They refer to genuine goods imported without the permission of the intellectual property rights holder but are legally purchased in another country.
They are undertaken by multinational companies as a dumping practice by selling excess inventory at lower prices in foreign markets.
They are associated with the import of counterfeit goods from unauthorized sellers, leading to trademark infringement.
They are a form of trade restriction where a country allows only authorized distributors to import foreign goods, protecting domestic markets from price fluctuations.
questions.e: Parallel imports (gray market goods) are branded goods imported into a market and sold without the trademark owner's consent. These goods are genuine and manufactured under license, not counterfeit, but are imported in contradiction to the brand owner's intent.

questions.q: Q.34) If a country is placed under the 'regular follow-up' category of the Financial Action Task Force (FATF), it implies:
o: the country is most likely to be placed in the 'grey list' in near future
the country is facing economic sanctions
the country is inefficient to manage illegal transactions
the country has taken positive measures to tackle money laundering
questions.e: "Regular follow-up" is the topmost category among FATF classifications. It indicates that a country, like India, has been lauded for its efforts to tackle illicit finance and implement measures against money laundering and terror funding.

questions.q: Q.35) Consider the following pairs — 1️⃣ Nostro account: Deposits are held in a foreign bank 2️⃣ Vostro account: Deposits are held in the currency of the country where the money is on deposit 3️⃣ Loro account: Deposits are maintained by one domestic bank for another in the form of a third party account
questions.e: Pair I is correct; Nostro refers to a bank's record of money on deposit at a foreign bank. Pair II is correct; Vostro accounts are maintained in the domestic currency. Pair III is correct; Loro is a current account maintained by one domestic bank for another as a third-party account.

questions.q: Q.36) With reference to trade and financial channels of exchange rates, consider the following — 1️⃣ The trade channel influences the exports and imports through changes in the prices of traded goods. 2️⃣ The financial channel describes how exchange rate movements influence the cost of foreign funding and investment. 3️⃣ Unlike the financial channel, which is sensitive to exchange rate changes against major currencies, the trade channel is more responsive to the trade-weighted exchange rate.
questions.e: The trade channel links fluctuations to export/import volumes via prices. The financial channel influences foreign funding and credit conditions. The financial channel is sensitive to major currencies like the USD/Euro, whereas the trade channel responds more to trade-weighted rates reflecting global competitiveness.

questions.q: Q.37) If the government needs to pay $10 million every month in interest on its current debt and if it devalues its currency, then:
o: the nominal interest payments are lowered
the real interest payments are increased but nominal interest payments remain unaffected
the trade deficit of the country would increase
the nominal interest payments are raised
