questions.e: If the government devalues its currency, nominal interest payments remain the same (e.g., $10 million/month). However, because the purchasing power of the currency is reduced, the real interest payments actually increase.

questions.q: Q.38) Which of the following are most likely impacts on the Indian economy if the US Federal Reserve cuts interest rates? — 1️⃣ Rise in foreign investment in India 2️⃣ Appreciation of Indian currency 3️⃣ Growth in the Indian share market
questions.e: Lower US rates incentivize global investors to invest in India's stocks and FDI. This increases confidence and aids momentum in the Indian stock market. It also leads to a weakening USD, potentially causing the Rupee to appreciate.

questions.q: Q.39) In the context of international trade, which one of the following is the primary objective of conducting a 'Principal Purpose Test' (PPT)?
o: To ensure that a business is not primarily created to avoid taxes by taking advantage of bilateral tax treaties
To check whether a foreign investment was made with a legitimate purpose or for obtaining speculative gains
To classify the goods in various categories for the application of rates of tariff on them
To determine the extent of inverted duty structure on specific commodities in an economy
questions.e: The PPT is part of the BEPS framework aimed at preventing misuse of tax treaties. It checks if a business arrangement was created mainly to avoid taxes; if so, treaty benefits can be denied.

questions.q: Q.40) India is a founding member of how many of the following? — 1️⃣ Asian Development Bank 2️⃣ Asian Infrastructure Investment Bank 3️⃣ African Development Bank Group 4️⃣ New Development Bank
questions.e: India is a founding member of the ADB  , the AIIB , and the New Development Bank. However, India is NOT a founding member of the African Development Bank, as it joined in 1983, years after its 1964 founding.

questions.q: Q.41) How many of the following are covered under the World Trade Organization (WTO) 'Agreements on Agriculture'? — 1️⃣ Jute 2️⃣ Forestry products 3️⃣ Tobacco products 4️⃣ Cotton
questions.e: The Agreement on Agriculture covers farm produce and processed products like Tobacco, Cotton, wool, and silk. It specifically excludes jute, rubber, sisal, fish/fishery products, and forestry products.

questions.q: Q.42) What is an "International Investment Position" of a country?
o: Percentage of GDP that comes from international investments in the country
Strategic international portfolio diversification of the country
Balance sheet of a country's external assets and liabilities
Ratio of Foreign Direct Investment (FDI) inflows to outflows in the country
questions.e: According to the IMF, the International Investment Position (IIP) is the balance sheet of the stock of external financial assets and liabilities. It includes claims on non-residents, liabilities to non-residents, gold, and SDRs.

questions.q: Q.43) How many of the following are included in India's external debt? — 1️⃣ Outstanding State credits, both defence and civilian 2️⃣ Special Drawing Rights allocations by the International Monetary Fund 3️⃣ Investments by foreign central banks in Treasury Bills 4️⃣ Floating Rate Notes
questions.e: India's external debt includes Rupee debt such as defense and civilian State credits , SDR allocations by the IMF , short-term debt like central bank investments in Treasury Bills , and commercial borrowings including Floating Rate Notes.

questions.q: Q.44) With reference to the 'Peace Clause' of the World Trade Organization (WTO), consider the following — 1️⃣ It states that a country can breach agricultural subsidy limits under the Agreement on Agriculture. 2️⃣ It is available to the developing nations till a 'permanent solution' is found by the WTO members to the issue of public stockholding for food security purposes.
questions.e: The Peace Clause protects developing countries from legal challenges if they breach agricultural subsidy limits (10% for India) while pursuing food procurement programs. It remains available until a permanent solution for public stockholding is found.

questions.q: Q.45) The Reserve Bank of India maintains gold reserves for how many of the following reasons? — 1️⃣ Balancing foreign exchange reserves 2️⃣ Hedging against fiat currencies 3️⃣ Preventing fluctuations in stock market prices
questions.e: RBI uses gold to balance foreign exchange reserves and provide stability to the currency. Gold also acts as a hedge against inflation and the eroding power of fiat currencies. However, gold reserves do not directly influence stock market prices, which depend on earnings and investor sentiment.

questions.q: Q.46) What is a Carry trade?
o: A situation where investors invest in a country's currency expecting its value to appreciate due to high interest rates.
A trade where investors buy and sell the same asset in different markets to profit from price differences.
A situation where the investors borrow money in a country where the interest rates are low and purchase assets in another country with higher returns.
A strategy where investors short sell a currency with high interest rates and buy a currency with low interest rates.
questions.e: Carry trade occurs when investors borrow money in a low-interest-rate country (like Japan) and invest it in a high-interest-rate country (like India or Brazil) to earn better returns.

questions.q: Q.47) In the context of Balance of Payment transactions, consider the following — 1️⃣ Accommodating Transactions are undertaken to cover deficit or surplus in Autonomous Transactions. 2️⃣ Cross border lending or borrowing cannot be undertaken as accommodating transactions.
questions.e: Statement I is correct; accommodating transactions are determined by the gap (surplus or deficit) left by autonomous transactions. Statement II is incorrect because official reserve transactions, which can include lending or borrowing by the central bank to bridge BoP gaps, are the primary accommodating items.

questions.q: Q.48) Which one of the following best describes the function of the World Integrated Trade Solution (WITS)?
o: Managing import and export permits for trade between countries
Forecasting currency exchange rates to assist in cross-border investment decisions
Analysing international trade and tariff data to assess trade flows and policies
Providing real-time data on international financial markets for global trade financing
questions.e: WITS is a collaborative effort allowing users to access data on international trade and trade protection. It provides tools to analyze regulations, tariffs, and market trends.

questions.q: Q.49) If another global financial crisis happens in near future, which of the following precautionary actions can be taken by India? — 1️⃣ Stricter Capital Adequacy Ratio (CAR) norms 2️⃣ Restricting Foreign Portfolio Investments (FPIs) 3️⃣ Increasing interest rates
questions.e: Precautionary actions include implementing stricter CAR norms (Basel III) to make banks resilient and increasing interest rates to reduce carry trade and avoid capital flight. However, opening up to MORE FPIs is not a precaution because FPIs are volatile and withdraw during crises.

questions.q: Q.50) Which one of the following terms is used to describe a situation where the currency moves quickly between financial markets to take advantage of short-term interest rate differences?
questions.e: Hot currency refers to funds that move quickly between financial markets to exploit short-term interest rate differences. Foreign portfolio investments are a common example of "hot money".

questions.q: Q.1) How many of the following activities form part of the capital market? — 1️⃣ Trading of Treasury Bills (T-Bills) 2️⃣ Long-term equity financing through stock exchanges 3️⃣ Call Money Market operations 4️⃣ Trading of Government Securities (G-Secs) with a maturity of 15 years
questions.e: The Capital Market is for borrowing and lending medium and long-term funds, generally above one year. This includes long-term equity financing and trading of long-term G-Secs. Treasury Bills and Call Money are short-term (under one year) and belong to the Money Market.

questions.q: Q.2) What is an 'Effective Capex'?
o: Capital Expenditure and the Grants-in-aid provided for creation of capital assets
Expenditure incurred in the current accounting year to create revenue in a future
Capital expenditure less the grant-in-aid for creation of capital assets
Capital expenditure less the depreciation value of the capital assets
questions.e: Effective Capital Expenditure is the sum of Capital Expenditure and Grants-in-Aid for the creation of Capital Assets (GIA Capital).

questions.q: Q.3) How many of the following can lead to a decrease in the bond yield? — 1️⃣ Increase in fiscal deficit 2️⃣ Increase in foreign investments in debt market 3️⃣ Increase in inflation
questions.e: Bond prices and yields are inversely related. Increased foreign investment increases demand/prices for bonds, thus decreasing the yield. Increased fiscal deficit or inflation typically leads to higher interest rates and higher bond yields.

questions.q: Q.4) Consider the following statements with regard to the External Commercial Borrowings (ECBs) in India — 1️⃣ Individuals are not permitted to raise ECBs. 2️⃣ They cannot be raised without prior approval from the Reserve Bank of India. 3️⃣ Existing ECBs cannot be refinanced by raising fresh ECBs.
questions.e: Statement I is correct; Individuals, Trusts, and NGOs are ineligible to raise ECBs. Statement II is incorrect; ECBs can be raised via the "automatic route" through banks, not just the "approval route" via RBI. Statement III is incorrect; existing ECBs can be refinanced if the fresh loan has a lower cost and maintains original maturity.

questions.q: Q.5) Which one of the following statements best describes the term Laffer Curve?
o: Tax revenue is maximized when the tax rate is made uniform for all income groups
Tax revenue is maximum when the taxes are fixed at an optimal rate
Tax revenue depends on the total number of taxpayers
Tax revenue increases when the taxes are fixed at higher rates
questions.e: The Laffer Curve shows that at both lower and higher tax rates, revenue is low; it reaches its maximum at an "optimal rate" where tax evasion is minimized.

questions.q: Q.6) How many of the pairs given above are correctly matched? — 1️⃣ Primary Deficit: Revenue deficit minus grants for capital assets 2️⃣ Fiscal Deficit: Total expenditure minus total receipts excluding borrowings 3️⃣ Effective Revenue Deficit: Indicates the government's borrowing from outside the country
questions.e: Pair II is correctly matched; Fiscal deficit is the difference between total revenue and total expenditure, excluding borrowings. Pair I is incorrect; Primary deficit is fiscal deficit minus previous interest payments. Pair III is incorrect; Effective Revenue Deficit is revenue deficit minus grants for the creation of capital assets.

questions.q: Q.7) If the tax multiplier is 1 in an economy, then 1 percent tax cut will lead to:
questions.e: The tax multiplier defines how a change in taxes affects GDP. In India, the tax multiplier is closer to 1, meaning a one-rupee tax cut provides a one-rupee boost to GDP.

questions.q: Q.8) Under which one of the following conditions does the incidence of an indirect tax fall more heavily on consumers than on producers?
o: When demand is more inelastic than supply
When the supply is more inelastic than demand
When the demand curve is perfectly elastic
When both supply and demand are equally elastic
questions.e: Tax incidence depends on price elasticity. When demand is inelastic, consumers are less responsive to price hikes and bear a larger share of the tax burden.

questions.q: Q.9) In the context of financial markets, which one of the following correctly describes the term "short-selling"?
o: Selling shares at a price lower than their intrinsic value to attract investors
Selling stocks immediately after purchase to book short-term profit
Selling underperforming shares from a long-term portfolio
Selling securities that one does not own, expecting to buy them back later at a lower price
questions.e: Short-selling involves borrowing a security to sell it, then buying it back later at a lower price to pocket the difference.

questions.q: Q.10) Statement I: Monetization of deficit can lead to demand pull inflation. Statement II: Monetization of the deficit can increase the money supply without corresponding economic output.
o: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct but Statement II does not explain Statement I
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Both Statement I and Statement II are correct and Statement II explains Statement I
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
questions.e: Monetisation (printing money to fund deficit) increases the money supply without more goods. This causes too much money to chase too few goods, leading to demand-pull inflation.

questions.q: Q.11) Which one of the following is not correct with regard to the Treasury Bills (T-bills)?
o: These can be purchased by the retail investors.
These can be issued both by the Central Government and the State Governments.
These are zero coupon securities and do not pay any interest.
These can be issued for a maturity period of less than a year.
questions.e: T-bills are exclusively issued by the RBI on behalf of the Union Government; State governments do not issue them. They are zero-coupon instruments issued at a discount with tenures of 91, 182, and 364 days.

questions.q: Q.12) How many of the pairs given above are correctly matched? — 1️⃣ Option: A right to buy/sell an asset within a certain time 2️⃣ Future: An agreement to buy/sell an asset at a predetermined price 3️⃣ Forward: A contract to exchange financial obligations based on a notional principal
questions.e: Pair I is correct; options provide the right but not the obligation to buy/sell. Pair II is correct; futures are standardized agreements to buy/sell at a predetermined price. Pair III is incorrect; "swaps" involve exchanging financial obligations based on a notional principal, while forwards are customized OTC contracts.

questions.q: Q.13) With reference to surcharge and cess in India's taxation system, consider the following — 1️⃣ Cess is a tax additionally levied as a percentage of existing tax amount. 2️⃣ Surcharge on income tax is shareable with the states. 3️⃣ Both the cess and surcharge cannot be used for purposes other than the purposes for which they are levied.
questions.e: Statement I is correct; cess is an additional tax for a specific purpose. Statement II is incorrect; surcharge is for the Union's use and is not shareable with states. Statement III is incorrect; while cess is for specific purposes , surcharge revenue goes into a general pool and can be used for any purpose.

questions.q: Q.14) Statement I: The government securities market is generally referred to as the gilt-edged market. Statement II: In the government securities, investors generally get assured returns.
o: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct but Statement II does not explain Statement I
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Both Statement I and Statement II are correct and Statement II explains Statement I
questions.e: Both statements are correct as G-Secs are safe, "gilt-edged" investments with assured returns. However, Statement II describes a feature of the securities rather than explaining why they are historically called "gilt-edged" (which is due to government backing and default safety).

questions.q: Q.15) How many of the following conditions lead to the emergence of an inflationary gap in an economy? — 1️⃣ Increase in the aggregate demand 2️⃣ Increased government expenditure 3️⃣ Lower levels of employment
questions.e: An inflationary gap occurs when actual GDP exceeds potential GDP due to high aggregate demand. This is caused by conditions like higher government expenditure. It is associated with elevated employment levels, not lower ones.

questions.q: Q.16) Consider the following statements — 1️⃣ While the GDP deflator includes only domestic goods, the Consumer Price Index (CPI) includes both domestic and foreign goods. 2️⃣ While the GDP deflator measures the prices of a fixed basket of goods and services, the Consumer Price Index (CPI) measures the prices of all goods and services.
questions.e: Statement I is correct; the GDP deflator covers only domestic goods, while CPI includes imports bought by consumers. Statement II is incorrect; it is the CPI that uses a fixed basket, whereas the GDP deflator measures all domestically produced goods/services.

questions.q: Q.17) With reference to Extra Budgetary Resources (EBRs) of the Government of India, consider the following — 1️⃣ They are financial liabilities raised by Public Sector Undertakings for which repayment of the entire principal and interest is done by the Central Government. 2️⃣ They are excluded from the Fiscal Deficit calculations, but are added to the total debt of the government.
questions.e: EBRs are liabilities raised by state-owned firms (PSUs) but repaid via the Government budget. They are excluded from official fiscal deficit calculations but included in total government debt.

questions.q: Q.18) How many of the pairs given above are correctly matched? — 1️⃣ Stagflation: Economic contraction in two consecutive quarters 2️⃣ Skewflation: Simultaneous occurrence of inflation and deflation 3️⃣ Reflation: Slow growth and a high unemployment rate
questions.e: Pair II is correct; Skewflation involves simultaneous inflation and deflation (Biflation) across sectors. Pair I is incorrect; Stagflation is slow growth with high unemployment and inflation. Pair III is incorrect; Reflation is a policy to expand output after a slowdown.

questions.q: Q.19) How many of the following are exempted from Goods and Services Tax (GST) in India? — 1️⃣ Research funding provided to State Universities 2️⃣ All the Cancer drugs 3️⃣ Distribution of electricity 4️⃣ Medical-grade oxygen
questions.e: Research funding for government universities and distribution of electricity are exempt. Cancer drugs are generally taxed at a reduced 5% rate (though 33 specific ones were recently zeroed ), and medical-grade oxygen is taxed at 5%.

questions.q: Q.20) A higher tax-to-GDP ratio denotes:
o: increase in the general price levels
increase in the current account deficit
questions.e: A higher ratio indicates a wider fiscal net and reduced dependence on borrowings, allowing the government to finance spending through revenue.

questions.q: Q.21) How many of the pairs given above are correctly matched? — 1️⃣ Sweat share: Issued to existing shareholders at a discounted price 2️⃣ Scrip share: Given to company employees without any charge 3️⃣ Preference share: Dividends are paid to shareholders prior to the issuance of common stock dividends 4️⃣ Right share: Given to existing shareholders without any charge
questions.e: Only Pair III is correct; preference shareholders receive dividends before common stockholders. Sweat shares go to employees. Scrip (bonus) shares go to existing shareholders for free. Right shares are offered to existing shareholders at a discount.

questions.q: Q.22) How many of the following steps can be taken by a government/central bank to tackle inflation in an economy? — 1️⃣ Decrease the repo rate 2️⃣ Increase the tax rates 3️⃣ Decrease public expenditure 4️⃣ Increase the import duty on raw materials
questions.e: Remediating inflation involves increasing tax rates to reduce spending and decreasing public expenditure (contractionary policy). Decreasing the repo rate increases money supply/inflation , and higher import duties can cause cost-push inflation.

questions.q: Q.23) Which one of the following best describes the term "Pump and Dump scheme"?
o: A strategy where traders sell borrowed stocks, expecting a price drop to buy them back at a lower rate
A monetary policy approach where the central bank lowers interest rates or injects liquidity during market downturns to prevent crashes
The practice of artificially inflating stock prices, only to sell them later at higher prices for profit
An illegal form of off-the-record stock trading where trades occur outside regulated stock exchanges
questions.e: This is a fraud where traders inflate prices with false info and sell at the peak, causing a crash.

questions.q: Q.24) How many of the pairs given above are correctly matched? — 1️⃣ Tobin tax: Sales tax 2️⃣ Ad valorem tax: Import duty 3️⃣ Pigouvian tax: Carbon emissions tax
questions.e: Pair II is correct; Ad valorem taxes like import duties are based on an item's value. Pair III is correct; Pigouvian taxes like carbon tax target harmful side effects. Pair I is incorrect; the Tobin tax is on currency conversions, not general sales.

questions.q: Q.25) Consider the following statements — 1️⃣ Deflation refers to a sustained decrease in the general price level of goods and services in an economy, leading to a negative inflation rate. 2️⃣ Disinflation refers to a slowdown in the rate of inflation. 3️⃣ Both disinflation and deflation are characterized by an overall decrease in the inflation rate.
questions.e: Deflation is a broad decline in prices (negative rate). Disinflation is a slowdown in the rate of increase. Both involve a decrease in the overall inflation rate.

questions.q: Q.26) Consider the following statements with regard to the Non-Convertible Preference shares — 1️⃣ They neither result in the expansion of the company's equity base or increase its debt. 2️⃣ They provide fixed dividends with a specified redemption period. 3️⃣ They do not provide the voting rights in the company's general meetings.
questions.e: Non-convertible preference shares do not carry voting rights. They don't expand equity or debt and pay fixed dividends until redemption.

questions.q: Q.27) Consider the following statements with reference to the Mutual Funds — 1️⃣ An equity mutual fund invests more than 60% of its total assets in equity shares. 2️⃣ Debt mutual funds are generally recommended to investors with lower risk tolerance.
questions.e: A fund is "equity" if >60% is in shares. Debt funds invest in bonds/G-Secs and are recommended for low risk tolerance.

questions.q: Q.28) Consider the following statements with regard to inflation targeting in India — 1️⃣ It is notified by the Central Government in consultation with the Reserve Bank of India (RBI). 2️⃣ India follows the Flexible Inflation Targeting (FIT) to maintain price stability.
questions.e: Targets are set by the government with the RBI every five years (currently 4% +/- 2%). India adopted FIT in 2016 for price stability.

questions.q: Q.29) Which of the following are derivative instruments? — 1️⃣ Futures 2️⃣ Promissory Notes 3️⃣ Credit Default Swaps 4️⃣ Commercial Paper
questions.e: Derivatives like futures and Credit Default Swaps derive value from underlying assets. Promissory Notes and Commercial Paper are debt/money market instruments.

questions.q: Q.30) In how many of the above rows is the given information correctly matched? — 1️⃣ CPI-AL: Labour Bureau - Base: 2005-06 2️⃣ WPI: Office of Economic Advisor - Base: 2011-12 3️⃣ IIP: National Statistical Office - Base: 2011-12 4️⃣ GDP Deflator: National Statistical Office - Base: 2005-06
questions.e: Pair II is correct; WPI is from the Economic Advisor with a 2011-12 base. Pair III is correct; IIP is from the NSO with a 2011-12 base. Pair I is incorrect; CPI-AL base is 1986-87. Pair IV is incorrect; GDP deflator base is 2011-12.

questions.q: Q.31) Statement I: A progressive income tax acts as an automatic stabiliser in an economy. Statement II: A progressive income tax makes consumer spending less sensitive to fluctuations in the GDP.
o: Statement I is incorrect, but Statement II is correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are correct, but Statement II does not explain Statement I
Both Statement I and Statement II are correct and Statement II explains Statement I
Statement I is correct, but Statement II is incorrect
questions.e: Progressive taxes act as shock absorbers because they take a higher share when incomes rise and less when they fall. This makes disposable income and spending less sensitive to GDP fluctuations.

questions.q: Q.32) How many of the following form part of the State Own Tax Revenue (SOTR)? — 1️⃣ Stamp Duty 2️⃣ Registration Fees 3️⃣ Motor Vehicle Tax 4️⃣ Security Transaction Tax 5️⃣ Corporation Tax
questions.e: SOTR includes stamp duty, registration fees, motor vehicle tax, sales tax, and SGST. Security Transaction Tax and Corporation Tax are collected solely by the Central Government.

questions.q: Q.33) Which one of the following refers to the provision to sell more shares than originally planned in an Initial Public Offering (IPO)?
questions.e: A greenshoe (over-allotment) option allows underwriters to sell up to 15% more shares than planned if demand is high.

questions.q: Q.34) Consider the following statements with regard to the Exchange Traded Funds (ETFs) — 1️⃣ They are investment funds traded on stock exchanges, similar to stocks. 2️⃣ They are priced once daily at the Net Asset Value (NAV). 3️⃣ They are regulated by the Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI).
questions.e: ETFs are traded on exchanges like stocks throughout the day. They are regulated by SEBI. Mutual funds are priced once daily at NAV, not ETFs.

questions.q: Q.35) Which of the following statements are correct with regard to inflation? — 1️⃣ Core inflation excludes products with volatile prices. 2️⃣ Both goods and services are included in the headline inflation. 3️⃣ Core inflation is measured to study the long term trend in the price rise.
questions.e: Core inflation excludes volatile food and fuel. Headline inflation covers all goods/services. Core inflation helps study long-term price trends for policy framing.

questions.q: Q.36) How many of the pairs given above are correctly matched? — 1️⃣ Tax buoyancy: Expenditure incurred on collection of taxes 2️⃣ Tax elasticity: Changes in tax revenue in response to changes in tax rate 3️⃣ Tax expenditure: Responsiveness of tax revenue growth to changes in Gross Domestic Product
questions.e: Pair II is correctly matched; elasticity measures revenue response to tax rate changes. Pair I is incorrect; buoyancy is the responsiveness of revenue growth to GDP. Pair III is incorrect; tax expenditure is revenue forgone via incentives.

questions.q: Q.37) Which one of the following refers to the practice of buying and selling the same security by the same investor to create misleading market information?
questions.e: Wash trading involves a trader buying and selling the same security to create an illusion of high volume and mislead the market.

questions.q: Q.38) Which one of the following statements best describes the term 'tax credit'?
o: It is a direct reduction in the amount of tax owed by an individual.
It is the process of taxing the income earned in another country.
It is the amount that can be deferred to future tax assessment years.
It is a deduction from the total income reducing the taxable income.
questions.e: A tax credit is subtracted directly from the taxes owed, making it more favorable than a deduction.

questions.q: Q.39) How many of the following facilitate the trade of Government Securities (G-Secs) in the Indian security market? — 1️⃣ National Stock Exchange (NSE) 2️⃣ Over-the-Counter (OTC) market 3️⃣ RBI's Retail Direct platform 4️⃣ NSE-goBID Platform
questions.e: Trade is facilitated through Stock Exchanges , the OTC market , RBI's Retail Direct platform , and platforms like NSE-goBID.

questions.q: Q.40) Mr. X is a salaried employee. In January 2018, he purchased SBI shares and sold them in April 2021 (held >36 months). The profit earned will be taxed under:
questions.e: Gains from transferring capital assets are taxed as Capital Gains. Since the holding period exceeded 36 months, it is classified as Long Term Capital Gains.

questions.q: Q.41) With reference to BSE SENSEX in India, consider the following — 1️⃣ It tracks the performance of the 100 largest companies in India. 2️⃣ It is always calculated in terms of Indian rupees. 3️⃣ It is reviewed and re-evaluated semi-annually each year.
questions.e: Statement III is correct; Sensex is reviewed semi-annually in June and December. Statement I is incorrect; it tracks the 30 largest/most active stocks. Statement II is incorrect; it is calculated in both Rupees and US Dollars.

questions.q: Q.42) Consider the following statements with regard to the lock-in period in capital market — 1️⃣ It is a duration after an IPO when certain shareholders are prohibited from selling their shares. 2️⃣ The end of the lock-in period can lead to a rise in the price of the shares.
questions.e: Statement I is correct; lock-in periods restrict certain shareholders from selling after an IPO. Statement II is incorrect; the end of the period usually causes a price drop due to a sudden influx of supply.

questions.q: Q.43) In the context of India's public finance, which one of the following best describes the term 'fiscal glide path'?
o: A strategy to reduce inflation by controlling money supply
A strategy to increase government spending gradually
A strategy to gradually reduce the fiscal deficit over time
A strategy to increase tax revenues
questions.e: The fiscal glide path is a strategic approach to gradually reduce the fiscal deficit over time to ensure manageable limits.

questions.q: Q.44) In which of the following ways does the 'Inverted Duty Structure (IDS)' impact an economy? — 1️⃣ It discourages domestic manufacturing by making raw materials costlier than finished goods. 2️⃣ It increases dependence on imports, leading to a higher trade deficit. 3️⃣ It discourages value addition.
questions.e: IDS occurs when duties on raw materials are higher than on finished goods. This discourages domestic manufacturing , increases import dependence/trade deficit , and hampers local value addition.

questions.q: Q.45) Which of the following is issued by the Government of India to meet the temporary mismatches in the government's cash flows and bridge the short-term liquidity needs?
questions.e: Cash Management Bills (CMBs) are short-term instruments issued to meet temporary cash flow mismatches.

questions.q: Q.46) How many of the pairs given above are correctly matched? — 1️⃣ Elephant Bond: Recover black money invested overseas 2️⃣ Impact Bond: Achieve social or environmental outcomes 3️⃣ Uday Bond: Take over the debts of the power distribution companies
questions.e: All three are correct. Elephant bonds aim to recover overseas black money. Impact bonds link payments to social/environmental outcomes. Uday bonds are issued by states to take over DISCOM debts.

questions.q: Q.47) Consider the following statements with reference to the capital receipts — 1️⃣ They create the sources of income contributing to the asset creation of the government. 2️⃣ Unlike disinvestment proceeds, which are non-debt capital receipts, special securities issued to public-sector banks are debt capital receipts.
questions.e: Statement II is correct; disinvestment proceeds are non-debt , while special securities to banks are debt capital receipts. Statement I is incorrect; capital receipts either create a liability or REDUCE an asset; they are not recurring income.

questions.q: Q.48) With reference to Participatory Notes (P-Notes), consider the following — 1️⃣ They are Offshore Derivative Instruments that allow foreign investors to invest in India. 2️⃣ Investors issuing P-Notes are required to register with Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI).
questions.e: Statement I is correct; P-notes are Offshore Derivative Instruments. Statement II is incorrect; they specifically allow investors to invest in Indian securities WITHOUT having to register with SEBI.

questions.q: Q.49) In which one of the following contexts the terms "Baa2 and Baa3" are mentioned?
questions.e: Baa2 and Baa3 are credit ratings (e.g., from Moody's) that assess the creditworthiness of a borrower.

questions.q: Q.50) Which of the following are categorised as negotiable instruments in India? — 1️⃣ Promissory Notes 2️⃣ Bills of Exchange 3️⃣ Cheques
questions.e: Negotiable instruments are transferable documents promising payment; common examples include Cheques, Bills of Exchange, and Promissory Notes.

questions.q: Q.1) Consider the following statements: 1️⃣ Water vapour is the primary driver of the Earth's current warming. 2️⃣ Water vapour is the most abundant greenhouse gas.
o: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct, but Statement II does not explain Statement I
Both Statement I and Statement II are correct and Statement II explains Statement I
Statement I is correct, but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect, but Statement II is correct
questions.e: Water vapor is Earth's most abundant greenhouse gas and is responsible for about half of Earth's greenhouse effect. However, it is not the primary driver of current warming; rather, it acts as a feedback mechanism that amplifies warming caused by other greenhouse gases like .

questions.q: Q.2) With reference to the temperature gradient, consider the following statements: 1️⃣ It is generally low over the tropical regions. 2️⃣ It is generally high over the eastern margins of continents. 3️⃣ Narrow spacing between isotherms indicates a high thermal gradient.
questions.e: The temperature gradient is the rate of change of temperature over distance. It is low in the tropics due to uniform solar heating. Narrow spacing of isotherms indicates a high gradient. Western margins typically have high gradients due to cold currents, while eastern margins have lower gradients due to warm currents.

questions.q: Q.3) With reference to jet streams, consider the following statements: 1️⃣ These are high-velocity, geostrophic winds that flow in the upper troposphere. 2️⃣ When the temperature contrast between air masses is maximum, the jet stream tends to flow in a nearly straight path.
questions.e: Jet streams are high-speed geostrophic winds in the upper troposphere. When the temperature contrast between air masses is at its peak (typically winter), the velocity is highest and the path is straight; when the contrast weakens, they meander into Rossby waves.

questions.q: Q.4) Consider the following statements: 1️⃣ Ocean Mean Temperature (OMT) is a more stable monsoon predictor than the Sea Surface Temperature (SST). 2️⃣ OMT often introduces short-term atmospheric "noise" that helps capture immediate monsoon-onset signals.
o: Statement I is correct, but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect, but Statement II is correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are correct, but Statement II does not explain Statement I
Both Statement I and Statement II are correct and Statement II explains Statement I
questions.e: OMT is a better predictor (80% accuracy) than SST (60%) because it measures heat content down to the  isotherm, making it stable against short-term fluctuations. SST is sensitive to immediate "noise" like wind and evaporation, which reduces its reliability.

questions.q: Q.5) With reference to geostrophic winds, consider the following statements: 1️⃣ They occur when the pressure gradient force is balanced by the Coriolis force. 2️⃣ They blow parallel to the isobars. 3️⃣ They correspond more closely to atmospheric winds over the oceans than over land.
questions.e: Geostrophic winds occur in the upper atmosphere where friction is absent, allowing a balance between the pressure gradient and Coriolis forces. They blow parallel to isobars. Because friction is lower over water, actual winds over oceans resemble geostrophic winds more closely than those over land.

questions.q: Q.6) Consider the following statements with regard to the Inter-Tropical Convergence Zone (ITCZ): 1️⃣ It is also referred to as the Horse Latitudes. 2️⃣ Well-defined warm and cold fronts are commonly observed in this region. 3️⃣ In the tropics, it results in the formation of the Hadley Cell. 4️⃣ At the equator, it results in two wet and two dry seasons each year, unlike in higher latitudes.
questions.e: The ITCZ is known as the doldrums, not horse latitudes (which are at  N/S). Fronts are characteristic of mid-latitudes, while the ITCZ is driven by convection. It forms the Hadley Cell. It produces two wet/dry seasons at the equator as it passes overhead twice a year.

questions.q: Q.7) With reference to tropical cyclones, consider the following statements: 1️⃣ Tropical cyclones derive most of their energy from the latent heat released during the condensation of water vapour. 2️⃣ The eye of a tropical cyclone contains the most intense winds. 3️⃣ Strong cyclones generally have a small eye.
questions.e: Energy comes from latent heat released during condensation. The eye is calm and warm; the strongest winds and heaviest rain are in the eyewall. As a cyclone intensifies, the eye contracts, leading to "pin-hole eyes" in strong storms.

questions.q: Q.8) Consider the following statements: 1️⃣ The amount of sunlight arriving at the top of Earth's atmosphere is only one-fourth of the total solar irradiance. 2️⃣ The lowest annual radiation rates in the high latitudes are recorded over their oceans. 3️⃣ The Equator receives less insolation compared to the tropics.
questions.e: Due to Earth's spherical shape and varying angles of incidence, the average top-of-atmosphere insolation is one-fourth of the solar constant. High-latitude oceans receive low radiation due to semipermanent cloud cover. The Equator receives less insolation than the subtropics because the latter have fewer clouds to block sunlight.

questions.q: Q.9) Consider the following statements: 1️⃣ A positive phase of the Pacific Decadal Oscillation (PDO) leads to an increased number of cyclones originating near the equator. 2️⃣ The positive phase of PDO is characterised by high sea surface temperature in the eastern Pacific Ocean.
o: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct, but Statement II does not explain Statement I
Statement I is incorrect, but Statement II is correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are correct and Statement II explains Statement I
Statement I is correct, but Statement II is incorrect
questions.e: During the positive PDO phase, the eastern Pacific warms and the western Pacific cools. This phase increases vertical wind shear and weakens low-level vorticity near the equator, which actually suppresses cyclone formation rather than increasing it.

questions.q: Q.10) Consider the following statements with regard to the dust particles in the atmosphere: 1️⃣ Their concentration is generally higher in the equatorial regions. 2️⃣ The blue colour of the sky is caused by the reflection of sunlight by these particles. 3️⃣ These particles generally enhance the Earth's albedo.
questions.e: Dust is higher in subtropics/temperate regions due to large deserts; equatorial humidity and rain remove dust. Rayleigh scattering by gas molecules (not dust) causes the blue sky. Dust generally increases albedo by reflecting solar radiation back to space, causing net cooling.

questions.q: Q.11) Consider the following statements with reference to the Extra-Tropical Cyclones: 1️⃣ Their strongest winds are typically found near the Earth's surface. 2️⃣ Unlike tropical cyclones, they possess a well-defined frontal system.
questions.e: Extra-tropical cyclones have their strongest winds near the tropopause (12 km up), whereas tropical cyclones have strongest winds near the surface. Extra-tropical cyclones are characterized by clear frontal systems (warm/cold fronts), which are absent in tropical cyclones.

questions.q: Q.12) Consider the following statements: 1️⃣ On 21st March, all the places on Earth experience exactly equal durations of day and night. 2️⃣ Atmospheric refraction bends incoming sunlight as it passes through the Earth's atmosphere.
o: Statement I is correct, but Statement II is incorrect
Both Statement I and Statement II are correct, but Statement II does not explain Statement I
Statement I is incorrect, but Statement II is correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are correct and Statement II explains Statement I
questions.e: While 21st March is an equinox, places do not experience "exactly" equal day and night because atmospheric refraction bends light, making the Sun visible before sunrise and after sunset. This makes daylight slightly longer than 12 hours everywhere on the equinox.

questions.q: Q.13) With reference to the Natal type of climate, consider the following statements: 1️⃣ It is found in both the Northern and Southern Hemispheres. 2️⃣ It receives rainfall from onshore trade winds all year round. 3️⃣ It serves as a primary formation zone for major tropical cyclones.
questions.e: The Natal type is found in both hemispheres (e.g., South Africa, SE USA, Australia). It differs from the China type by receiving trade-wind rainfall year-round. It is a warm temperate climate; tropical cyclones originate over warmer tropical waters (>), so this is not a primary formation zone.

questions.q: Q.14) Consider the following statements: 1️⃣ Places situated at higher elevations generally experience lower temperatures compared to places located near sea level. 2️⃣ The atmosphere is primarily heated from below by long-wave terrestrial radiation.
o: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct, but Statement II does not explain Statement I
Statement I is correct, but Statement II is incorrect
Both Statement I and Statement II are correct and Statement II explains Statement I
Statement I is incorrect, but Statement II is correct
questions.e: The atmosphere is heated from below as the Earth's surface absorbs solar radiation and re-emits long-wave radiation. Temperature drops with altitude (lapse rate) because air moves further from this heat source and undergoes adiabatic cooling due to lower pressure.

questions.q: Q.15) With reference to Western Disturbances, consider the following statements: 1️⃣ They are cyclonic circulations that occur in the middle and lower tropospheric levels. 2️⃣ They induce low-pressure systems in the lower layers of the atmosphere. 3️⃣ They play a beneficial role in supporting rabi crop production in north India.
questions.e: Western Disturbances are cyclonic circulations in the mid-lower troposphere. They induce low pressure in lower layers, bringing winter rain to plains and snow to hills. This moisture is vital for early growth of rabi crops like wheat and mustard.

questions.q: Q.16) Consider the following characteristics: 1️⃣ It receives summer rainfall from easterly winds coming from the ocean. 2️⃣ Its predominant vegetation is cool temperate forest. 3️⃣ It is primarily found along the eastern coasts of Africa and Australia. 4️⃣ Fishing is an important economic activity in this region. How many of the above statements are NOT characteristic features of the Cool Temperate Eastern Margin Climate?
questions.e: The Cool Temperate Eastern Margin (Laurentian) climate is found in N. America and East Asia, not Africa or Australia. Thus, statement III is incorrect. Statements I (summer rain from easterlies), II (cool temperate forests), and IV (fishing, e.g., Grand Banks) are all correct.

questions.q: Q.17) Consider the following statements: 1️⃣ The Arabian Sea remains relatively cooler than the Bay of Bengal. 2️⃣ Remnants of typhoons originating in the western Pacific Ocean often enter the Bay of Bengal and re-intensify into cyclonic systems. 3️⃣ The trough-like structure of the Bay of Bengal promotes air convergence and vertical uplift, aiding rapid cyclone intensification once a depression develops. Which of the factors given above explains the higher incidence of cyclones in the Bay of Bengal as compared to the Arabian Sea?
questions.e: All three factors explain the difference: the Bay is warmer (), whereas the Arabian Sea is cooled by dry winds; Pacific typhoons often re-intensify in the Bay ; and the Bay's geomorphology aids convergence.

questions.q: Q.18) Consider the following statements: 1️⃣ High salinity suppresses evaporation from the ocean surface. 2️⃣ Warm western boundary currents contribute to high evaporation zones in subtropical oceans.
questions.e: Salinity reduces the vapor pressure of water, requiring more energy for molecules to escape, thus slowing evaporation. High evaporation occurs over subtropical belts where warm western boundary currents like the Gulf Stream raise water temperatures.

questions.q: Q.19) Consider the following: 1️⃣ Siberian 2️⃣ Mediterranean 3️⃣ Savanna 4️⃣ Steppe. How many of the climate regions given above receive rainfall throughout the year?
questions.e: Only the Siberian climate has rainfall fairly well-distributed throughout the year. Mediterranean climate has dry summers; Savanna has distinct wet and dry seasons; Steppe has minimal winter precipitation.

questions.q: Q.20) With reference to the Indian Ocean Dipole (IOD), consider the following statements: 1️⃣ It is the result of the difference between the temperature south of Indonesia and in the Arabian Sea. 2️⃣ A positive IOD obstructs the progression of monsoon rainfall over India. 3️⃣ A negative IOD results in a higher-than-normal number of cyclones in the Bay of Bengal. How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: IOD is the temperature difference between the western (Arabian Sea) and eastern (south of Indonesia) Indian Ocean. Statement I is correct. Positive IOD actually enhances monsoon flow and increases rainfall over India. Negative IOD leads to stronger cyclogenesis in the Bay of Bengal. Statements I and III are correct.

questions.q: Q.21) Consider the following statements: 1️⃣ Anabatic winds are caused by pressure-driven convection, whereas katabatic winds are controlled by temperature and elevation differences. 2️⃣ While anabatic winds occur during the day, katabatic winds are stronger particularly at night.
questions.e: Anabatic winds are upslope winds driven by daytime solar heating/pressure convection. Katabatic winds are downslope winds driven by surface cooling and gravity, often peaking at night when cooling is most intense.

questions.q: Q.22) Consider the following statements: 1️⃣ Convection plays a significant role in the formation of dew. 2️⃣ Conduction is primarily responsible for the development of cumulonimbus clouds. 3️⃣ Advection is a key process for the formation and behaviour of local wind systems.
questions.e: Dew forms via radiational cooling and conduction; stable air that suppresses convection is needed. Cumulonimbus clouds require intense convection, not just conduction. Advection (horizontal air movement) is the basis of local winds like land/sea breezes.

questions.q: Q.23) Consider the following statements: 1️⃣ Vertical winds in the atmosphere are generally much weaker than horizontal winds. 2️⃣ A strong vertical pressure gradient is balanced by the downward pull of gravity.
o: Statement I is correct, but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect, but Statement II is correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are correct, but Statement II does not explain Statement I
Both Statement I and Statement II are correct and Statement II explains Statement I
questions.e: Hydrostatic balance occurs when the upward pressure-gradient force is cancelled by gravity, keeping vertical motions weak. Horizontal winds, driven by pressure gradients and Coriolis force, are thus much stronger.

questions.q: Q.24) Consider the following pairs: 1️⃣ Stratocumulus - Net cooling 2️⃣ Cirrus - Net warming 3️⃣ Cumulonimbus - Neutral. Which of the pairs given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Low, thick clouds like stratocumulus reflect solar radiation, causing cooling. High, thin cirrus clouds trap outgoing longwave radiation, causing warming. Cumulonimbus clouds have both strong albedo and greenhouse effects that roughly offset each other.

questions.q: Q.25) Consider the following statement: 1️⃣ Volcanic eruptions can act as a natural fertilizer for oceans. 2️⃣ Volcanic ash is rich in nutrients, such as iron, that are used by phytoplankton.
o: Statement I is correct, but Statement II is incorrect
Both Statement I and Statement II are correct and Statement II explains Statement I
Both Statement I and Statement II are correct, but Statement II does not explain Statement I
Statement I is incorrect, but Statement II is correct
questions.e: Volcanic ash contains iron, a vital micronutrient for phytoplankton. When deposited in iron-limited ocean regions, it stimulates blooms and increases biological productivity.

questions.q: Q.26) Consider the following statements with regard to cold fronts: 1️⃣ They are characterised by the appearance of cirrus clouds, followed by altocumulus clouds. 2️⃣ They generally produce moderate precipitation over a large area for several hours.
questions.e: The approach of a cold front is marked by high-level cirrus followed by thicker altocumulus. Precipitation at the front itself is intense and localized (cumulonimbus) rather than moderate and large-scale.

questions.q: Q.27) Consider the following statements: 1️⃣ Mackerel Sky refers to the visual appearance created by cirrocumulus clouds. 2️⃣ Mares' tail refers to high-altitude, wispy cirrus clouds resembling a horse's tail.
questions.e: Mackerel sky describes cirrocumulus clouds that resemble fish scales or water ripples. Mares' tails are wispy, ice-crystal cirrus clouds high in the troposphere that look like horse tails.

questions.q: Q.28) Consider the following statements: 1️⃣ Most of the hot deserts are found along the western part of the continents between 15 to  north and south of the Equator. 2️⃣ Tropical easterly winds bring rain to the eastern margins of the continents. 3️⃣ Cold ocean currents flow along the western coasts of the continents. Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
o: Both Statement II and Statement III are correct, but only one of them explains Statement I
Only one of the Statements II and III is correct and that explains Statement I
Neither Statement II nor Statement III is correct
Both Statement II and Statement III are correct and both of them explain Statement I
questions.e: Hot deserts are on western margins because trade winds (easterlies) become dry by the time they reach those coasts and blow offshore. Cold ocean currents on western coasts further stabilize air and prevent rain. Both explain the arid western margins.

questions.q: Q.29) With reference to the Madden-Julian Oscillation (MJO), consider the following statements: 1️⃣ It is an equatorial, eastward-travelling pattern of anomalous tropical rainfall. 2️⃣ It is observed mainly over the Indian Ocean and the Pacific Ocean. 3️⃣ It is called a '30-60 day oscillation' based on the time period of each cycle.
questions.e: MJO is a planetary-scale pattern of tropical rainfall moving eastward near the equator. It is primarily identifiable over the Indian and Pacific Oceans due to warm sea temperatures. Each cycle lasts roughly 30-60 days.

questions.q: Q.30) Arrange the following biomes in increasing order of average world productivity: 1️⃣ Savanna 2️⃣ Tropical Rainforest 3️⃣ Temperate Forest 4️⃣ Temperate Grassland 5️⃣ Taiga 6️⃣ Tundra.
questions.e: Productivity (NPP) is lowest in Tundra (harsh cold) and highest in Tropical Rainforest (warm/wet). The order is Tundra < Temperate Grassland < Taiga < Savanna < Temperate Forest < Tropical Rainforest.

questions.q: Q.31) Consider the following pairs: 1️⃣ Cirrus - Always composed of ice crystals 2️⃣ Nimbostratus - Result from the thickening of altostratus clouds 3️⃣ Altostratus - Produce a halo phenomenon 4️⃣ Stratus - Low-level layers with a fairly uniform grey or white colour. How many of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
questions.e: Cirrus clouds are always ice crystals. Nimbostratus forms as altostratus thickens. Stratus is a uniform low-level grey layer. Pair III is wrong; halos are a feature of cirrostratus, while altostratus does not produce them.

questions.q: Q.32) Consider the following information regarding Local Winds: 1️⃣ Sirocco - United States of America 2️⃣ Bora - Siberia 3️⃣ Pampero - Argentina 4️⃣ Simoom - Eastern Sahara. In how many of the above rows is the given information correctly matched?
questions.e: Pampero is a cold wind in the Argentinian Pampas. Simoom is an intense hot/dry wind in the Arabian/Eastern Sahara deserts. Sirocco is a Saharan wind blowing toward the Mediterranean, not the USA. Bora blows from Hungary toward Italy, not Siberia.

questions.q: Q.33) Consider the following characteristics of a biome: 1️⃣ It is generally treeless due to extremely low temperatures and a very short growing season. 2️⃣ It contains soils with significant organic matter accumulation because decomposition is slow. 3️⃣ It is found in high-latitude regions with permafrost conditions. The biome described above is:
questions.e: The Tundra is a treeless biome with a short growing season (50-60 days) and permafrost. Cold temperatures result in very slow organic decomposition, leading to a buildup of soil carbon.

questions.q: Q.34) Consider the following statements regarding the Mediterranean climate region: 1️⃣ It is not found in the African continent. 2️⃣ It experiences rainfall in summers due to the prevailing Trade Winds. 3️⃣ The region is generally a net exporter of citrus fruits but net importer of dairy products.
questions.e: Mediterranean climate is found in Africa (e.g., Cape Town). Summers are hot and dry because offshore trade winds block rain. It is a net exporter of citrus but net importer of dairy because poor grass quality limits cattle rearing.

questions.q: Q.35) Consider the following statements: 1️⃣ The Subtropical Jet (STJ) Stream plays a significant role in the onset of the Indian summer monsoon. 2️⃣ In summer, a STJ Stream positioned south of the Himalayas strengthens low-pressure conditions over north-west India.
o: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct and Statement II explains Statement I
Both Statement I and Statement II are correct, but Statement II does not explain Statement I
Statement I is incorrect, but Statement II is correct
Statement I is correct, but Statement II is incorrect
questions.e: The STJ's shift is crucial for the monsoon. In winter/summer, as long as it stays south of the Himalayas, its associated subsidence maintains stable high-pressure and dry weather, preventing the monsoon despite surface low pressure. It must move north for the monsoon to start.

questions.q: Q.36) Consider the following statements: 1️⃣ Meteorological drought refers to a deficiency in precipitation relative to the long-period average (LPA). 2️⃣ In India, over half of the geographical area is considered drought-prone. 3️⃣ The Ministry of Earth Sciences is the nodal Ministry for monitoring and managing drought conditions in India.
questions.e: Meteorological drought is a rainfall deficit vs LPA. About 68% (over half) of India is drought-prone. The Ministry of Agriculture and Farmers' Welfare, not Earth Sciences, is the nodal ministry.

questions.q: Q.37) Consider the following statements with regard to Adiabatic Lapse Rate (ALR): 1️⃣ A Dry ALR refers to the rate at which rising air cools with no heat exchange. 2️⃣ A positive ALR leads to the development of thunderstorms, tornadoes, and cyclones.
questions.e: Dry ALR is the cooling rate of unsaturated air () without external heat exchange. A positive ALR (temp decrease with height) allows parcels to rise, cool, and release latent heat, which fuels severe weather systems.

questions.q: Q.38) Consider the following statements: 1️⃣ Ozone depletion over Antarctica intensifies during the polar winter. 2️⃣ Extremely cold temperatures lead to the formation of Polar Stratospheric Clouds (PSCs) within the polar vortex.
o: Statement I is incorrect, but Statement II is correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are correct, but Statement II does not explain Statement I
Both Statement I and Statement II are correct and Statement II explains Statement I
Statement I is correct, but Statement II is incorrect
questions.e: Winter cold in the polar vortex forms PSCs. These clouds facilitate the creation of reactive chlorine radicals that rapidly destroy ozone once sunlight returns, making depletion most intense when the vortex is strong.

questions.q: Q.39) Absolute humidity is defined as:
o: the ratio of water vapor to dry air by volume
the maximum water vapor the air can hold at a given temperature
the percentage of moisture relative to the air's maximum capacity
the actual amount of water vapor per unit volume of air
questions.e: Absolute humidity is the actual mass of water vapor present in a unit volume of air, usually expressed in grams per cubic meter.

questions.q: Q.40) Consider the following statements with regard to cloudbursts: 1️⃣ These are generally associated with cumulonimbus clouds. 2️⃣ These are commonly seen in areas with large horizontal temperature gradients.
questions.e: Cloudbursts occur in cumulonimbus clouds when strong updrafts hold moisture until it is suddenly released. They are driven by vertical instability and orographic uplift, not horizontal temperature gradients.

questions.q: Q.41) Which of the following cloud types are typically responsive to cloud seeding? 1️⃣ Cumulus clouds 2️⃣ Stratiform clouds 3️⃣ Cirrus clouds.
questions.e: Cloud seeding requires supercooled liquid water. Vertically developed cumulus and layered stratiform clouds have this water and are responsive. Cirrus clouds consist of ice crystals and lack the liquid water needed for seeding.

questions.q: Q.42) Arrange the following surfaces in decreasing order of their albedo: 1️⃣ Old snow 2️⃣ Desert 3️⃣ Thick clouds 4️⃣ Asphalt 5️⃣ Crops.
questions.e: Albedo values are: Thick clouds (70-80%), Old snow (45-50%), Desert (30-45%), Crops (10-25%), and Asphalt (5%).

questions.q: Q.43) With reference to El-Niño Modoki, consider the following statements: 1️⃣ It leads to the development of an anomalous two-cell Walker Circulation over the tropical Pacific. 2️⃣ The Arabian Sea tends to experience a higher frequency of cyclones during the pre- and post-monsoon seasons.
questions.e: El-Niño Modoki features central Pacific warming that creates a two-cell Walker Circulation. It suppresses cyclones in the Bay of Bengal while increasing their frequency in the Arabian Sea during pre- and post-monsoon periods.

questions.q: Q.44) With reference to local winds in India, consider the following statements: 1️⃣ Norwesters are quite beneficial for pre-kharif crops such as jute and paddy. 2️⃣ Elephanta refers to the post-monsoon south-easterly winds blowing along the Malabar Coast. 3️⃣ Blossom showers are post-monsoon showers in Kerala.
questions.e: Norwesters (Kalbaisakhi) provide vital rain for pre-kharif jute and paddy. Elephanta are post-monsoon winds on the Malabar Coast in Sept-Oct. Blossom showers are pre-monsoon (March-April) rains that help coffee plants.

questions.q: Q.45) Match the following climatic groups with their characteristics: 1️⃣ Humid Continental - Winter dry season 2️⃣ Tropical Wet and Dry - No dry season, warm summer 3️⃣ Humid Subtropical - No dry season, severe winter.
questions.e: Based on Koeppen's scheme: Humid Continental (Df) has no dry season and severe winters. Tropical Wet and Dry (Aw) has a winter dry season. Humid Subtropical (Cfa) has no dry season and warm summers.

questions.q: Q.46) Why are the Roaring Forties stronger in the Southern Hemisphere?
o: The Southern Hemisphere has higher mountain ranges that channel and intensify the winds.
Lower air pressure at high southern latitudes compared to northern latitudes increases wind speed.
The Coriolis force is stronger in the Southern Hemisphere, accelerating westerly winds.
The Southern Hemisphere has less landmass, allowing winds to flow unimpeded over vast oceans.
questions.e: Large landmasses in the Northern Hemisphere block and weaken the Westerlies. In the Southern Hemisphere, the vast expanse of ocean between  and  allows these winds to blow with much greater force and regularity.

questions.q: Q.47) Which of the following atmospheric situations is/are associated with the formation of 'Heat Domes' over a region? 1️⃣ Stationary high-pressure system 2️⃣ Clear skies 3️⃣ A stationary jet stream.
questions.e: A heat dome occurs when a stationary high-pressure system traps warm air. Descending air suppresses cloud formation, leading to clear skies. This happens when a meandering jet stream becomes stationary, holding the high-pressure system in place.

questions.q: Q.48) Consider the following statements with regard to the Rossby Waves: 1️⃣ They are prominently developed along the Intertropical Convergence Zone (ITCZ). 2️⃣ They occur in both the atmosphere and the oceans owing to the rotation of the Earth. 3️⃣ Their meandering can lead to equatorward penetration of cold polar air and poleward transport of warm tropical air.
questions.e: Rossby waves form due to Earth's rotation; this effect is minimal near the equator, so they do not develop in the ITCZ. They exist in both oceans and the atmosphere. Meandering transports cold polar air toward the equator and warm tropical air toward the poles.

questions.q: Q.49) With reference to Equatorial Plasma Bubbles (EPBs), consider the following statements: 1️⃣ They are ionospheric phenomena. 2️⃣ They disrupt high-frequency radio waves. 3️⃣ In general, EPBs occur most frequently during equinoxes.
questions.e: EPBs are depleted plasma pockets in the ionosphere. They scatter radio signals, disrupting HF communication and GPS. They generally peak during equinoxes, though regional variations exist.

questions.q: Q.50) In which one of the following layers of the atmosphere are the highest temperatures recorded?
questions.e: The Thermosphere attains the highest temperatures (thousands of degrees Celsius) as sparse molecules absorb high-energy solar X-rays and UV rays. However, it wouldn't feel hot to a human because the air is too thin to transfer much heat.

questions.q: Q.1) Consider the following statements: 1️⃣ The Earth has a variable magnetic field generated by convective currents. 2️⃣ A permanent magnet cannot exist at Earth's core due to the extremely high temperatures. 3️⃣ Earth's magnetic field is the result of convection in the inner core combined with the Coriolis effect.
o: Both Statement II and Statement III are correct, but only one of them explains Statement I
Only one of the Statements II and III is correct and that explains Statement I
Both Statement II and Statement III are correct and both of them explain Statement I
Neither Statement II nor Statement III is correct
questions.e: Earth's magnetic field is generated by convective currents in the liquid outer core, not the inner core. High temperatures in the core (above ) make a permanent magnet impossible as magnets lose properties at such heat. Thus, only Statement II is correct and explains why the field must be dynamic (Statement I).

questions.q: Q.2) Consider the following statements: 1️⃣ There is an observed daily delay in moonrise. 2️⃣ Earth undergoes an additional angular rotation each day to compensate for the Moon's eastward orbital progression.
o: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct, but Statement II does not explain Statement I
Statement I is correct, but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect, but Statement II is correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are correct and Statement II explains Statement I
questions.e: The Moon orbits Earth eastward. Because the Moon moves in its orbit while Earth rotates, Earth must rotate a bit further (about 50 minutes extra) each day to realign with the Moon, causing the daily delay in moonrise.

questions.q: Q.3) Consider the following statements with regard to the ocean currents: 1️⃣ The Leeuwin Current along Western Australia is a cold current that supports extensive coral reef ecosystems. 2️⃣ The Agulhas Current meets the Benguela Current near the Cape of Good Hope, creating zones of upwelling and high marine productivity. 3️⃣ The Oyashio Current flows southward along Japan's eastern coast, bringing cold, nutrient-rich waters. 4️⃣ The Canary Current induces downwelling along the Moroccan coast, hampering the fisheries industry.
questions.e: The Leeuwin Current is a warm current, not cold. The Agulhas Current is a warm current that meets the cold Benguela Current, creating rich biodiversity. The Oyashio is a cold subarctic current. The Canary Current causes upwelling (not downwelling) and supports highly productive fishing zones.

questions.q: Q.4) Consider the following statements: 1️⃣ The Tropics ( to ) are the only latitudes where the Sun can reach the zenith during the year. 2️⃣ The angle between Earth's rotational axis and the plane of the ecliptic is approximately .
o: Statement I is correct, but Statement II is incorrect
Both Statement I and Statement II are correct but Statement II does not explain Statement I
Both Statement I and Statement II are correct and Statement II explains Statement I
Statement I is incorrect, but Statement II is correct
questions.e: Due to Earth’s  axial tilt, the Sun’s declination only oscillates between the Tropics. This tilt means the axis makes a  angle with the ecliptic plane. This geometry ensures the Sun is only ever directly overhead (at zenith) within the tropical zone.

questions.q: Q.5) Consider the following countries: 1️⃣ Indonesia 2️⃣ Malaysia 3️⃣ Papua New Guinea 4️⃣ Philippines 5️⃣ Australia. Which of the above are part of the region called 'Amazon of Seas'?
o: I, II, III and IV only
questions.e: The "Amazon of the Seas" refers to the Coral Triangle, which includes Indonesia, Malaysia, Papua New Guinea, the Philippines, Solomon Islands, and Timor-Leste. Australia has rich coral but is not part of the core Coral Triangle region.

questions.q: Q.6) Consider the following statements with regard to Gyres: 1️⃣ The Coriolis effect causes gyres to rotate clockwise in the Southern Hemisphere and counterclockwise in the Northern Hemisphere. 2️⃣ Ekman transport plays a key role in the development and maintenance of gyres.
questions.e: In the Northern Hemisphere, gyres rotate clockwise, and in the Southern Hemisphere, they rotate counterclockwise. Statement I is reversed. Ekman transport is central to gyre formation as it converges water, creates a pressure gradient, and initiates geostrophic flow.

questions.q: Q.7) Consider the following statements with regard to Meridians: 1️⃣ Unlike parallels of latitude, all meridians are equal in length. 2️⃣ The distance between meridians decreases toward the poles. 3️⃣ The intersection of the zero-degree meridian and the zero-degree parallel is known as Null Island.
questions.e: All meridians are equal length because they all span the distance between the two poles. Meridians converge at the poles, so the distance between them is smallest there. The  coordinate is colloquially called Null Island.

questions.q: Q.8) Consider the following statements: 1️⃣ The Philippine Island Arc has formed due to the convergence of the Philippine Sea Plate and the Eurasian Plate. 2️⃣ Mount Fuji is situated at the convergence between the Pacific Plate and the Eurasian Plate. 3️⃣ Hot spot volcanism occurs primarily at the plate convergence zones where one plate subducts beneath another.
questions.e: The Philippine Island Arc is a convergent boundary where the Philippine Sea Plate subducts beneath the Eurasian Plate. Mount Fuji is at a complex triple junction including the Pacific and Eurasian plates. Hot spot volcanism occurs in the interior of plates, away from boundaries.

questions.q: Q.9) Consider the following statements: 1️⃣ The liquid nature of the Earth's outer core was inferred well before direct evidence was available. 2️⃣ The S-waves completely disappear and the P-waves slow down at the Gutenberg Discontinuity.
o: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct and Statement II explains Statement I
Statement I is incorrect, but Statement II is correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are correct but Statement II does not explain Statement I
Statement I is correct, but Statement II is incorrect
questions.e: Scientists inferred the liquid outer core from indirect seismic observations because no direct samples exist. At the Gutenberg Discontinuity (2900 km), P-waves slow down and S-waves disappear (as they cannot travel through liquid), proving the core is liquid.

questions.q: Q.10) Consider the following statements: 1️⃣ A coastal country exercises full sovereignty over the water column, airspace, seabed, and subsoil of its Territorial Sea. 2️⃣ A coastal country may presume as unlawful any removal of archaeological or historical objects from the seabed of its Contiguous Zone without its consent. 3️⃣ Land-locked countries may conduct marine scientific research in another country's Exclusive Economic Zone without permission, provided the research is non-commercial.
questions.e: Coastal states have sovereignty over the 12 nm Territorial Sea. In the Contiguous Zone (up to 24 nm), states can control the removal of archaeological objects. However, research in an EEZ always requires the coastal country's consent.

questions.q: Q.11) Consider the following: 1️⃣ Tombolo 2️⃣ Arete 3️⃣ Inselberg 4️⃣ Chasms. How many of the above are depositional landforms?
questions.e: Only Tombolo is a depositional landform (marine). Arete is a glacial erosional feature. Inselberg is a wind erosional feature. Chasms are marine erosional features.

questions.q: Q.12) Which one of the following is identified as the most probable source of energy for the occurrence of plutonism and volcanism on Earth?
questions.e: Primordial heat (from Earth's inception) and radiogenic heat (from radioactive decay) are the major drivers of internal energy, leading to the melting of mantle rocks and causing volcanism.

questions.q: Q.13) Match the following seismic zones with their associated areas: 1️⃣ Most active - Rann of Kutch 2️⃣ Second most active - Delhi 3️⃣ Moderately active - Odisha 4️⃣ Least active - Karnataka.
questions.e: Zone V (Most active) includes the Rann of Kutch. Zone IV (Second most) includes Delhi. Zone III (Moderately active) includes Odisha. Zone II (Least active) includes Karnataka.

questions.q: Q.14) Consider the following statements with regard to Canyons: 1️⃣ These are formed by river erosion as well as tectonic activity. 2️⃣ These are typically steeper and narrower than gorges. 3️⃣ Gandikota Canyon, the 'Grand Canyon of India,' is carved by the Penna River.
questions.e: Canyons form from river erosion and tectonic uplift (e.g., Grand Canyon). Gorges are actually steeper and narrower than canyons. Gandikota in Andhra Pradesh is carved by the Penna River.

questions.q: Q.15) Consider the following statements with regard to the Acidic Lava: 1️⃣ These are low-viscosity lavas with a high melting point. 2️⃣ These have a high percentage of silica and are of low density. 3️⃣ These give rise to felsic igneous rocks such as granite and rhyolite.
questions.e: Acidic lavas are highly viscous (sticky), not low-viscosity. They are silica-rich and low density. They form rocks like granite and rhyolite. Statement I is incorrect.

questions.q: Q.16) Consider the following information: 1️⃣ Hamada - Sahara Desert - Bare rocks 2️⃣ Reg - Taclamacan Desert - Pebbles 3️⃣ Erg - Thar Desert - Sand dunes 4️⃣ Bolson - Chihuahuan Desert - Depression. In how many of the above rows is the given information correctly matched?
questions.e: Only row II is correctly matched for Reg. Row I is incorrect because Hamada is bare rock, but the location example provided in the source is Libya. Row III is incorrect as the example provided for Erg is in Libya or Turkestan. Row IV is incorrect because Bolson is a depression, but the description given in the table for Row IV matches Hamada.

questions.q: Q.17) A desert research team identifies a landform characterized by: 1️⃣ A normally dry, steep-sided valley created by episodic, high-energy flash floods 2️⃣ Occasional flow from exotic streams fed by distant snowmelt 3️⃣ Vertical corrasion leading to pronounced incision. Which of the following landforms best fits the description?
questions.e: Wadis are dry channels deepened by vertical corrasion during occasional cloudbursts and can host exotic streams from distant snowmelt.

questions.q: Q.18) Consider the following information: 1️⃣ Tectonic - Titicaca - Peru/Bolivia 2️⃣ Rift valley - Tanganyika - Kenya 3️⃣ Cirque - Red Tarn - Sudan 4️⃣ Caldera - Scutari - Montenegro/Albania. In how many of the above rows is the given information correctly matched?
questions.e: Row I is correct. Row II is incorrect; Tanganyika borders Burundi, DRC, Tanzania, and Zambia, not Kenya. Row III is incorrect; Red Tarn is in England, not Sudan. Row IV is correct; Scutari is on the Montenegro/Albania border.

questions.q: Q.19) Consider the following: 1️⃣ It occurs when large slabs of rock are stripped away 2️⃣ It is caused by the release of confining pressure 3️⃣ It is common in granite domes. What is this type of weathering?
questions.e: Exfoliation (or sheeting) involves peeling slabs of rock due to pressure release, common in granite domes.

questions.q: Q.20) Consider the following statements with regard to spring tides: 1️⃣ The Earth-Moon-Sun alignment during these tides is the same as the alignment that occurs during eclipses. 2️⃣ They occur twice a month all year long. 3️⃣ Their high tides are a little lower and low tides are a little higher than average.
questions.e: Spring tides occur when the Sun, Moon, and Earth align (syzygy), which is the same as eclipse alignment. They happen twice a month (full and new moon). They have higher than average high tides and lower low tides, not the other way around.

questions.q: Q.21) Which one of the following best describes Secular Variation in Earth's magnetic field?
o: Long-term, gradual change over decades to centuries
questions.e: Secular variation is the long-term, gradual change in magnetic declination caused by fluid processes in the outer core.

questions.q: Q.22) Match the following types of sand dunes: 1️⃣ Seif - One wing 2️⃣ Star - Pyramid-like, multi-armed 3️⃣ Parabolic - U-shaped, anchored by vegetation 4️⃣ Barchans - Crescent-shaped, tips face downwind.
questions.e: Barchans are crescent-shaped with wings away from the wind. Parabolic dunes form where vegetation anchors sand. Seif dunes have only one wing. Star dunes are pyramid-shaped with multiple arms.

questions.q: Q.23) Consider the following: 1️⃣ In the Arctic and Antarctic regions, a distinct thermocline layer is not present throughout the year. 2️⃣ At higher latitudes, surface and deep waters show little variation in temperature, salinity, or density.
o: Statement I is incorrect, but Statement II is correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are correct and Statement II explains Statement I
Both Statement I and Statement II are correct, but Statement II does not explain Statement I
Statement I is correct, but Statement II is incorrect
questions.e: In polar regions, surface water is already near , meaning there is no temperature contrast with deep water. Without this contrast or density variation, no thermocline forms.

questions.q: Q.24) Consider the following: 1️⃣ Rakhine Yoma Mountains 2️⃣ Java Trench 3️⃣ Altai Mountains 4️⃣ Somali Plate. How many of the above define the geographical boundaries of the Indian Plate?
questions.e: The Rakhine Yoma (East) and Java Trench (Southeast) define Indian Plate boundaries. The Altai Mountains and Somali Plate are separate tectonic features.

questions.q: Q.25) Consider the following statements with regard to lithification: 1️⃣ It transforms unconsolidated sediments into sedimentary rocks. 2️⃣ It does not involve recrystallization of minerals within the rock. 3️⃣ Schist and slate are rocks formed through this process.
questions.e: Lithification turns loose sediment into sedimentary rock. It can involve recrystallization during compaction. Schist and slate are metamorphic, not sedimentary.

questions.q: Q.26) Consider the following: 1️⃣ Earthquakes occurring along Mid-Ocean Ridges are relatively low in magnitude. 2️⃣ Mid-Ocean Ridges are formed at the divergent plate boundaries.

questions.e: Diastrophism includes orogenic (mountain building), epeirogenic (continental building), and earthquake processes. Volcanism is considered a separate endogenic process.
